name: cloud-superapp

app.what: the fleet roster this phone sees

description: Diego's Cloud SuperApp — modularized monolith Android app. Single APK, gradle multi-module: app/ (launcher shell) + libs/{core,mail,cal,feed,net,ops,vault,chat}/ (independent feature modules). FairEmail-derived mail with JMAP, CalDAV/Radicale calendar, RSS, WireGuard tunnel, cloud ops dashboard, vault. Build via Nix devShell (gradle + AGP + Android SDK), one APK out.

android._doc_abi_filters: Native-library ABIs shipped in the APK. Defaults to arm64-v8a only because MapLibre Native (added in Push 2) ships ~15-18MB of .so per ABI; shipping all 4 default ABIs (arm64-v8a + armeabi-v7a + x86 + x86_64) inflates the APK from ~22MB to ~82MB. Every Samsung Galaxy from S8 (2017) onward + every modern Pixel is arm64, so this is safe for the user's device. To support 32-bit devices or x86 emulators, add 'armeabi-v7a' / 'x86_64' to this list and rebuild — no Kotlin / gradle edits needed.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, cloud-myterminal, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD telling you to use the one shared key — it never generates or substitutes a random/legacy key.

diagnostics._doc: On-device DevControlServer diagnostics → cloud sink + local download. Baked into BuildConfig.LOG_SINK_URL / LOG_SINK_STREAM by app/build.gradle. log_sink_url is our OpenObserve (the Loki-equivalent log store, openobserve on oci-apps) ingest, reached via the PUBLIC first-party analytics collector so NO credential is embedded in the public APK (the collector relays to openobserve server-side). '{stream}' in the url is replaced with log_sink_stream at runtime. EMPTY url = cloud push disabled (the 'Download logs' action still works fully); set it to the confirmed collector ingest path to enable one-tap 'Send logs to cloud'. Data-driven: change here, every app rebuild picks it up — never hardcode in Kotlin.
diagnostics._doc_log_ingest: Endpoint for DevControl → 'Send to cloud' (libs:core LogUpload.post). DISTINCT from log_sink_url: that one relays a structured stream to OpenObserve, this one POSTs a raw logcat dump as {source, log} to c3-infra-api's registerPublicLogsRoutes, which writes <source>-<epoch>.log under PUBLIC_LOGS_DIR and answers {ok, file}. EMPTY ON PURPOSE, same convention as log_sink_url: the API route exists (POST /public/logs) but nothing publishes it to the internet — the Caddy edge allowlists only /pub/health, /pub/ready and /pub/analytics/*, and everything else under /pub/* demands a Bearer, which is exactly the credential a log-reporting path must not need. Filling in a plausible URL would make the button fail with a 403 that looks like a phone problem. To enable: add an unauthenticated handle for the logs route in the caddy Caddyfile alongside /pub/analytics/*, then set this to the resulting URL. LogUpload.post already reports a blank endpoint as 'no log endpoint configured' rather than pretending to send.

emulator._doc: build.sh emulator boots an arm64 AVD for FULL-FIDELITY testing of the arm64-v8a APK — the emulator emulates arm64 wholesale (TCG/software on this x86_64 host: slow but faithful), so NO libhoudini translation is involved (unlike the Waydroid path). The emulator binary + system image come from the Nix devShell (flake.nix composeAndroidPackages includeEmulator/includeSystemImages). system_image ABI+API MUST match flake.nix abiVersions/systemImageTypes/platformVersions. avd_name is created idempotently by build.sh from system_image; boot_args are passed verbatim to `emulator`.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Bump here, rebuild devShell.
toolchain._doc_sdk_bump: compile_sdk bumped 34→35 to satisfy androidx.health.connect:connect-client:1.1.0-alpha10's AAR metadata constraint (it requires consumers to compile against Android 35+ for the new HC permission definitions wired to API 35 constants). AGP 8.5.2 maxes at compileSdk 34, so AGP bumped 8.5.2→8.7.3 (first stable AGP supporting compileSdk 35). Gradle 8.7→8.10.2 follows AGP 8.7's Gradle 8.9+ requirement. target_sdk stays at 34 — opting into Android 15 runtime behaviour is a separate concern from compiling against its APIs.
toolchain._doc_heliboard_bump: compile_sdk bumped 35→36 + the whole toolchain re-pinned to vendor HeliBoard main as libs:keyboard (self-contained keyboard provider). HeliBoard main pins AGP 8.13.2 / Kotlin 2.3.20 / Gradle 8.14 / compileSdk 36 (Android 16) / NDK 28.0.13004108, and uses the standalone Kotlin 2.0 Compose-compiler plugin (org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose) — so app + libs:wallet dropped composeOptions.kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion in favour of that plugin. nixpkgs channel bumped 24.11→25.05 because 24.11's androidenv/kotlin/gradle predate API 36 / Kotlin 2.3 / Gradle 8.14. target_sdk unchanged. See libs/keyboard/README.md.

constellation._doc: Fleet members regen.sh cannot discover by scanning this monorepo's siblings. Declared as DATA rather than hardcoded in the script (FIRE RULE #6). CORRECTED 2026-08-31: every URL here used to point at cloud-infra-desktop and 404'd, because this entry was never updated when the app was MOVED into this repo by cloud-infra-desktop commit 204da3397 ('hand devices to cloud-android'), which also deleted ship-cloud-infra-desktop-termux-boot.yml. It now lives at a_solutions/ae-tool_termux-boot/ and ships from here via .github/workflows/ship-termux-boot.yml. The GitHub Release asset is the REQUIRED channel and is anonymously pullable; the ghcr_page/image below is best-effort and may 404 or answer private (the package was created through the PAT path before the 2026-08-28 per-package token fix), so nothing load-bearing may depend on it. FUTURE OPTION, deliberately not taken in this edit: a_solutions/ae-tool_termux-boot/build.json already declares android.application_id + release.ghcr, so widening the scan root to a_solutions/ would let it self-register and this hand-maintained entry — exactly the thing that went stale — could be deleted.
constellation._doc_groups: Constellation tabs, in the order they render (#343). StoreCloudFragment draws one tab per group below that has at least one row, then appends Perms; it names no group itself. regen.sh stamps every fleet entry with a group: group_members[<fleet id>] when declared, otherwise the group whose default_for_kind matches the entry's kind. An entry whose kind has no default, a member naming an undeclared group, a member id that is not in the fleet, or an id used twice fails the regen instead of silently landing a row in the wrong tab. Tiny-ML = extreme edge and microcontroller models under about 2MB; Lite-ML = mobile and desktop CPU models, roughly 5MB-50MB. ORDER (#383): the owner asked for Lite-ML before Tiny-ML, so Lite-ML is declared first — the tab row IS this array's order. The two ids are IDENTITY: #343 created them and nothing may rename one to follow a label or a position, so the swap moves objects and touches no key.

groups.label: Apps
groups.blurb: Full constellation apps — install, update, open, remove.

groups.label: Libs
groups.blurb: One APK per library module, installable and inspectable on its own. Most are also compiled into the apps that use them. Two are not: net-wg (WireGuard), an out-of-process engine its app needs installed, and the two rootfs libraries — the ~400 MB root filesystems the terminals enter (#628). Those two are large, and they are ordinary: the store installs and updates them exactly like every other row here, and the terminal that needs one reads it out of the installed APK instead of downloading a runtime of its own.

groups.label: Lite-ML
groups.blurb: Lite-ML: mobile and desktop CPU models, roughly 5MB-50MB. Real modules install like any lib and are engines the keyboard needs installed. Reference rows have nothing to install; Update all never fetches them.

groups.label: Tiny-ML
groups.blurb: Tiny-ML: extreme edge and microcontroller models, under about 2MB. Reference rows are third-party libraries with nothing to install; Update all never fetches them.

constellation._doc_ml_naming: #405. AN ML LIB SAYS SO IN ITS OWN NAME, AND THAT NAME IS THE ONLY PLACE IT IS SAID. Every ML entry — real module or reference row — is named ml-{t|l}-{domain}-{name}: t = Tiny-ML, l = Lite-ML, domain = the application the model serves (voice, text, image, sensor, tabular). A scanned lib module carries the store's lib- row prefix in front of it, so its fleet id is lib-ml-l-voice-vosk; a catalogue row is written that way directly. regen.sh derives the tab from the name (the t-or-l segment of an id matching ^lib-ml-{t|l}- names the tab, libs-t-ml or libs-l-ml) and StoreCloudFragment derives the application heading from the same name's domain segment, so the tab, the heading and the name cannot disagree — there is nothing left to keep in sync. This REPLACED group_members, a hand-written {fleet id -> tab} map: it stated three things, and all three are now either derived (the two engines name their own weight class) or unnecessary. keyboard-engines was the third. It is Cloud-Keyboard-Libs.apk (~55MB arm64), the companion APK that BUNDLES the two engines, and it was pinned into Lite-ML for that reason; the owner asked for it back in Libs, because the engines it bundles are already their own installable rows and listing the bundle beside them counted the same ML twice. It now takes the libs default for kind lib by saying nothing at all. THE WEIGHT-CLASS CRITERION is the groups[].blurb size rule, applied to measured numbers: Vosk + JNA ship ~25MB of .so per ABI (keyboard-engines/build.json::android._doc_abi_filters) and each small Vosk model is a further ~40-50MB download (build.json::voice._doc); ML Kit bundles no .so at all but downloads a model per language pair. Both clear the 2MB Tiny-ML ceiling by more than an order of magnitude, so the large gap between them does not place them in different tabs — both are l. libs:voice and libs:translate are NOT ML and keep their plain names: they are the engine INTERFACES and their build.gradle files carry no ML runtime, which is the test test-constellation-groups.sh T2/T7 actually measure. libs:keyboard is not a fleet entry.
constellation._doc_catalogue: REFERENCE ROWS, not buildable modules (#343): third-party ML libraries listed so the Tiny-ML and Lite-ML tabs describe what exists, with no APK, package, image or release asset. regen.sh emits them into constellation-fleet.json's top-level `catalogue` array, never into `apps`, and stamps each installable:false itself. Fleet.parse reads only `apps`, so the updater, both auto-update workers, PrivilegedGrants and the recovery screens can never be handed an entry with no package. StoreCloudFragment draws them as blocked rows, which Fleet.installAllLocked drops before it checks status, so no batch fetches one or counts it as a failure.

upstreams._doc: Workspace tracking clones of upstream FOSS apps. Each lives at ../ea_<domain>-<project>/ (gitignored, see _dotfiles/git/src/gitignore ea_*-*/ rule). Refresh with `git -C ../ea_<x>-<y> pull`. Code is cherry-picked into libs/<domain>/ — NEVER built as a gradle subproject directly (they're top-level apps, not libraries).

kde-connect.license: GPL-2.0 (UPSTREAM REFERENCE ONLY — we do NOT vendor it)
kde-connect._doc_phase: CLEAN-ROOM, SELF-CONTAINED. libs/kde-connect is an ORIGINAL implementation of the KDE Connect LAN protocol written by us (NetworkPacket framing, mutual-TLS handshake with a self-signed device cert, protocol-v8 encrypted identity re-exchange, cert-pinned pairing, plugin registry: ping/clipboard/findmyphone/notification). The KDE repo above is consulted ONLY for the documented interop FACTS (port 1716; the TCP-dialer is the TLS server; pairing = trust-the-cert) — those are functional protocol requirements, not copyrightable expression. NONE of KDE's GPL-2.0 source is copied/vendored, so the app keeps its own license. Connects over wg0 by explicit wg_ip (auto-discovery can't cross WireGuard). Next: a foreground service hosting an inbound TCP server (1716-1764) so peers can also initiate, plus battery/share/mpris plugins.

firewall.license: Apache-2.0 (UPSTREAM REFERENCE ONLY — not vendored in v1)
firewall._doc_phase: CLEAN-ROOM, SELF-CONTAINED (v1). libs/firewall is ORIGINAL code: a minimal no-root per-app outbound firewall. A local VpnService captures traffic into a tun; ALLOWED apps are added via addDisallowedApplication() so they bypass the tunnel onto the real network, while BLOCKED apps fall into the tun and their packets are dropped (no forwarding loop) — zero root, zero native code. The RethinkDNS repo above (Apache-2.0, Kotlin) is consulted ONLY as the cherry-pick source for FUTURE complex tooling (DoH/DoT/DNSCrypt filtering, per-connection tracker, WireGuard proxying via its Go firestack engine). NO upstream source is copied/vendored in v1, so the app keeps its own license. Single VPN slot: while the firewall holds the device VPN slot, the libs:net WireGuard tunnel cannot run; unifying them is the first firestack cherry-pick. Sync the reference clone with: ./build.sh sync-firewall.

firestack._doc: MOVED, NOT DUPLICATED. The real firestack declaration is ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json::firestack — libs/firewall/build-firestack.sh, fetch-firestack.sh and publish-firestack.sh all read it there, and the module owns its engine's config because libs:firewall has TWO consumers (this app and lib-apks). What used to sit here was a STALE COPY of that block: it still declared repo/ref against celzero's `n2` branch after the tree became an owned clone, and its tracker named ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/firewall/firestack-src, a directory that does not exist and never did on this branch. Nothing read any of it — verified by grep for .firestack readers on 2026-09-10 — so it could only ever mislead the next reader, which it did: the brief for this task was written from it. Kept as this pointer rather than deleted outright so a search for firestack in the app that consumes it still lands somewhere true.

ops._doc_no_upstream: ops is a thin c3-api dashboard — no FOSS upstream to fork. Will be original code.

core._doc_no_upstream: core is shared infra (DB, theming, prefs, the updater) — original code.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh. Until this block existed the 34 testers under test/ were run only by hand by agents — the ship workflow called assembleRelease and nothing else — so a tester nobody's workflow called was indistinguishable from no tester at all.

shell._doc_requires: Tools a tester shells out to. Checked BEFORE anything runs, because a missing tool does not fail a tester — it makes the tester answer from the tool's absence. test-no-conflict-markers.sh assigns HITS=$(rg ...) and passes when HITS is empty: with no rg on PATH it certifies a tree that has conflict markers in it, and this was demonstrated by planting one. test-comms-tile-retarget.sh's absent() helper does the same in reverse. Both discard stderr, so 'command not found' never appears. Naming the tools here converts that silent green into a loud red.
shell._doc_quarantine: Filename → the REASON it may fail. Enumerated and visible, NOT a blanket tolerance: a quarantined tester that starts PASSING fails the build, so an entry cannot outlive its reason. Anything not named here is fatal.

unit._doc: Robolectric suite under app/src/test/. #512: BottomNavSelectedPillTest inflates the REAL activity_main and asserts the RESOLVED bottom-nav (itemBackground id, measured pill bounds, rendered pixel) — the selected pill vanished for a whole release while every XML-text tester stayed green, so this widget is proven on the inflated view or not at all. One module only: the shared libs run their own suites in ab_cloud-libs-shared.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list. Adding a new feature module = one entry here + mkdir + minimal build.gradle.

app.comment: Launcher / shell. Hosts navigation to each feature module.

libs:web-core._doc: #1371 THE embedded web view: CloudWeb.create(ctx, WebProfile.X), profiles, GPU probe, render-process recovery, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:auth.comment: #587 THE sign-in of the fleet, shared BY REFERENCE with cloud-drive: the four declared ways in (Authelia bearer, Authelia web-auth, GitHub and Google device grant), the artifact fetches, the vault route, the registry and the journey state machine, plus the Compose surface Profile > Connect hosts for step 1. Reads ONE declaration: ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json::auth.

libs:bottomnav.comment: THE bottom nav of the fleet, in Compose, shared BY REFERENCE (#565/#531). The shell hosts it through BottomNavIslandView in activity_main; ShellBottomNav feeds it ui.bottom_nav. There is no private nav left in this tree.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ui-kit.comment: #773 THE shared Compose kit of the fleet, shared BY REFERENCE: CloudKitTheme over the launcher palette roles (LauncherPalette.kit), section header, selectable tile, card, settings/switch rows, confirm dialog, and the View-interop shims KitComposeFragment / Context.kitComposeView a page migrates through.

libs:search.comment: The search ENGINE, app-agnostic and UI-free: matching, one section per scope in the declared order, the scope chips' rule and per-entry defaults (SearchEntry), the ":"-command line. The app supplies hits, live lookups and commands through SearchSource and draws the results itself (search/SearchPanel.kt). Reads ui.search_scopes from the CONSUMING app's build.json into its own BuildConfig.

libs:core.comment: Shared models, DB, theming, prefs, auth. No domain logic.

libs:databackend._doc_dir: #825 the engine wire (IDataBackend + DataBackendClient/Service), out of libs:core so a wire edit rebuilds only the engines and the apps that bind one.

libs:fleet-endpoints._doc_dir: #1093 the fleet endpoint fallback (plain JVM), shared with Cloud Mail and Cloud Account: libs:account links it (`api`), and this app hosts libs:account, so the graph must include it. The SuperApp declares no fleet_endpoints, so nothing is routed here.

libs:fleet-endpoints-android._doc_dir: #1093 the Android halves of the fleet endpoint design; libs:account links it (`api`) and this app hosts libs:account.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc_dir: #825 the fleet-config manifest + migration policy (FleetPolicy), out of libs:core: compiled by this app (it plans and diffs the whole fleet) and the Cloud-Lib-Fleetconfig engine every other app's provider asks over IPC.

libs:sysdns._doc_dir: #874 FleetDnsBridge: app/build.gradle links this module as the one resolver of this process (1f36254d4), so settings.gradle must include it — this map is the gradle graph's single source of truth, and a dependency missing here is 'Project with path :libs:sysdns could not be found' at configuration time.

libs:text-tools._doc: The ITextTools binder, shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ exactly as cloud-mail links it. This app CALLS it; cloud-keyboard serves it. Configs ▸ AI ▸ Tokens Fleet is the only consumer here, and what it wants across the boundary is the keyboard's AI-Routing state — which models its registry holds, which one is chosen, whether a provider key is set. Linking the binder is what makes that a question this app can ask at all; without it there is no channel from cloud-superapp to another app's routing settings.
libs:text-tools._doc_not_the_engine: This does NOT bring AiRouter, TextEnhancer or the registry into this app. Those stay in libs:keyboard, in the keyboard's process, and cloud-superapp deliberately does not link libs:keyboard — it is an IME with an ndk-build native decoder and a Compose settings tree, and a launcher does not take that as a dependency to read a model list. Everything Tokens Fleet shows is read over the binder from the app that owns it, which is also why there is no second copy of the model registry here to go stale.

libs:updater.comment: In-app auto-updater. Periodic WorkManager check against ghcr.io via OCI HTTP API (same flow build.sh phone-install uses). If remote sha256 differs from current PackageInfo's, installs it. Fleet.commit prefers the shell channel (uid 2000 holds INSTALL_PACKAGES → `pm install` with NO confirm dialog and no Play Protect scan prompt), falling back to PackageInstaller (which prompts) when no channel is live. All knobs in release.auto_update — no hardcoded URLs.

libs:appstore._doc: The Store (#563; formerly the Constellation store): fleet list, install/update actions, background pass. Split from the app so store, launcher and updater are separable - libs:updater is the engine, this is the storefront. UI, so it cannot go out-of-process like libs:net; the win is the boundary.

libs:shared-store._doc_dir: cloud-shared-store's store-access layer (contract). libs:appstore compiles it for the generated ICloudExec client: SharedUidMigration asks the OLD terminal build to back its home up over CLOUD_EXEC. Shared BY REFERENCE; reads ac_cloud-termux/build.json::shared_store.

libs:account._doc: #867 Account (the Profile page: Connect, Fleet cockpit, Infos, Drift, business card) as a library, so SuperApp and the Cloud Account app host one code path. The host supplies its palette, tab chrome, icons, router, haptics and mesh tunnel through AccountHost.

libs:mail.comment: Mail — FairEmail-derived, JMAP-extended. Source upstream: github.com/M66B/FairEmail (GPLv3). Tracking clone lives at ../ac_mail-fairmail/.

libs:ops.comment: Cloud ops dashboard — c3-api, health checks, dagu trigger, container control.

libs:chat.comment: Chat / messaging. Likely integrates with mattermost-bots (chat.diegonmarcos.com) — could fork Mattermost-Mobile / SimpleX / Conversations later.

libs:health.comment: MyHealth — native Android Health Connect dashboard. Reads aggregated records (Steps, Distance, Floors, Elevation, HR, RHR, HRV, VO2max, BP, BloodGlucose, SpO2, Temperature, RespiratoryRate, Sleep+stages, Exercise, Weight/BodyFat/Lean/Bone/Water, Hydration, Nutrition, Cycle) via androidx.health.connect:connect-client. All of Garmin Connect / Google Fit / Samsung Health / Fitbit / Oura sync INTO Health Connect on-device — single SDK gets the union. LOCAL-ONLY: persists rollups + caches into HealthStore (libs:core, SharedPreferences). Zero network. No OAuth, no webhooks, no cloud ingester. The Compose PAGES moved to ac_cloud-me (Projects > Health) and the SuperApp no longer routes to any of them; the module stays because Configs > Permissions uses HealthMetrics + HealthConnectGateway to count and request the Health Connect grants. Taxonomy still read from build.json::ui.sections[id=health].metrics.

modules._libs_browser_tombstone: libs:browser MOVED to ac_cloud-browser (constellation APK). Removed from app.depends_on and from this module list 2026-07. The Tools tile target is now extapp:cloud-browser. launchUri http/https now sends ACTION_VIEW to com.diegonmarcos.cloudbrowser instead of instantiating BrowserHostFragment.
modules._libs_fin_tombstone: libs:fin MOVED to ac_cloud-me (Buro > Fin). Removed from app.depends_on and from this module list, along with ui.myfin_mock — MyFinDashboardFragment had exactly one referrer here (SectionPages' `myfin` dispatch) and that section is gone. The Cloud tile that deep-linked to it (Projects Me ▸ MyFin, extapp:cloud-me#page:buro/fin) has since been dropped by the owner as well, so nothing in this app targets Buro > Fin any more — it is reached from inside Cloud-Me. settings.gradle derives the gradle module graph from this map, so dropping the entry is what actually removes :libs:fin from the build.

libs:launcher-apptabs.comment: App Tabs — last-6 opened SuperApp entries (sections, pages, external apps) rendered as a 2-col GRID. Sister module to libs:browser; same card-grid UX, different content (sealed Entry: SectionEntry | PageEntry | ExternalAppEntry). AppTabPrefs is SharedPreferences-backed ('app_tabs' file, strict LRU cap=6). Producers call AppTabPrefs.recordSection / recordPage / recordExternalApp on every successful navigation; the GRID re-renders on onResume so flipping back to Tabs always shows the freshest LRU. AppTabsHost is the callback interface MainActivity implements to handle card-tap re-navigation without libs:launcher-apptabs reaching back into app/.

libs:kde-connect.comment: KDE Connect (Configs > KDE page). FULLY SELF-CONTAINED, CLEAN-ROOM — our own implementation of the KDE Connect LAN protocol, no org.kde.kdeconnect_tp dependency and NO KDE GPL source vendored. Pipeline: dial <wg_ip>:1716 over wg0 → write identity (plaintext) → mutual-TLS handshake AS the TLS server (BouncyCastle self-signed device cert; the dialer is the TLS server per the protocol) → re-exchange identity encrypted (v8) → cert-pinned pairing (KdeTrustStore) → NetworkPacket plugins (ping/clipboard/findmyphone/notification). Data-driven from ui.kde_connect (self_name + devices[].wg_ip); nothing hardcodes an IP. BouncyCastle (bcpkix/bcprov jdk15to18) is the only added dep, for cert generation. Next phase: foreground service + inbound TCP server so peers can initiate too.

libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools.comment: Shizuku ADB debug tools — makes the SuperApp a SELF-CONTAINED 'adb shell' surface. A Shizuku UserService (IShellService.aidl + ShellUserService) runs in SHELL context (uid 2000) when Shizuku is running + granted, so it executes arbitrary `dumpsys` / `getprop` / `cat /sys/...` that the app's own uid + the SELinux-hardened proc/sys path can't reach (One UI 7+/Pixel A15+ block /sys/class/power_supply/*). ShizukuAdb is the binder facade (bindBlocking + exec + grantDump self-grant of android.permission.DUMP via `pm grant`). AdbDiagnostics runs DATA-DRIVEN command bundles declared in build.json::shizuku_diagnostics.bundles[] (charger/usb/battery/thermal/pd) and returns them as JSON. Exposed over the loopback DevControlServer at /api/adb/* (token-gated). This is the path that finally surfaces the USB-PD/PPS negotiation needed to debug 'why is the charger at 3W not 35W'.

libs:firewall.comment: No-root per-app outbound firewall. v2 = data-driven conditional per-app rules (FirewallRules/FirewallDecider/FirewallConditions, presets in assets/firewall_presets.json); interim drain-engine (FirewallVpnService). Phase 3 will consume the firestack netstack aar (flatDir libs/firewall/firestack/, `implementation(name:'firestack', ext:'aar')`) to run WG + per-app filtering + IN/OUT in one VpnService. Surfaced in About under Battery (info rows + 'Firewall Details' → FirewallDialog master switch + per-app preset picker).

libs:battery.comment: Battery/energy engine + its dialogs, extracted from app so it sits as a sibling of libs:firewall. Tier-1 (no-root): BatteryManager/sysfs correlation. Tier-2 (privileged): ShizukuEnergy reads `dumpsys batterystats` via the Shizuku user-service (IUserService/ShizukuUserService) now consolidated into libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools — hence the lib→lib dep (not lib→app). Consumed by app/devcontrol (the About UI). Also the 'battery-manager' for per-app energy ranking (EnergyWatchdog.perAppEstimate) feeding the Phone 'Top Battery' smart folder. THE battery Source of Truth lives here too: BatteryRepository (reads + records into battery_sot.db on battery events and the 15-min tick) → BatteryTruth.compute (one report) → BatteryRows (the words); the Battery badge, the home-screen battery popup and Configs ▸ About ▸ Battery (page:config/battery) all draw that report.

libs:light.comment: The Light tool (#1155) shared by reference: LightModel (rules, plain Kotlin), LightAndroid (torch, clock, prefs, the Off-action foreground service, manifest-merged) and LightPanel (the Compose page). The SuperApp's LightActivity and Cloud Calc's Toolkit > Light page both draw LightPanel over the one Light engine; the engine's rules are tested in app/src/test/.../light/LightEngineTest.kt.

libs:perms.comment: #1274 the permission contract: the catalogue asset (perms-catalogue.json: every runtime / special / app-op / adb-only grant with its SDK window, exact settings page, highlight key, adb line and the features that need it), the live status reader, the settings opener, the auto-request batch planner, the ADB block generator, PermsNeeds and the PermsLink deep link. Feature libs (wifi, bluetooth) use it to show a banner that opens the host's Permissions page; they never ask themselves. Renders nothing.

libs:bluetooth.comment: #1221 Android Bluetooth as one shared lib: scan with filters and RSSI, connect, bond, GATT discovery, read / write / notify / indicate, descriptors, MTU, known-service decoding from the declared UUID catalog (assets/bluetooth/gatt-catalog.json), the ATT log and the Dev tools, and the five-tab Compose page (BluetoothPanel). The SuperApp draws it in Configs > Fleet > Bluetooth (BluetoothFragment); Cloud Browser's Web Bluetooth polyfill (#1222) drives the same GattSession. Runtime permissions are in the lib manifest. Its rules are tested in app/src/test/.../bluetooth/.

libs:wifi.comment: #1263 the Wi-Fi analyzer as one shared lib, app-agnostic (the host injects WifiHostConfig; this app passes build.json wifi_analyzer): WifiManager scans within the throttle, ScanResult parsing (channel math, width, standard, security / PMF / WPS, 802.11mc / az, MLO), the IEEE OUI vendor table and regulatory channel plans as assets, channel rating, the connected link (ConnectivityManager / LinkProperties / WifiInfo), RTT ranging, network tools (ping, traceroute, DNS, port scan, NSD / SSDP / sweep / NetBIOS discovery, throughput), heatmap, roaming log, CSV / JSON / PCAP export, and the five-tab Compose page (WifiPanel). The SuperApp draws it in Configs > Setup > Network > WiFi (WifiFragment); Cloud Calc embeds the same panel. Its rules are tested in app/src/test/.../wifi/.

libs:datamanager.comment: The 'data-manager' — pure per-app DATA providers, no UI. AppUsageProvider (UsageStatsManager: recency / active-window / launch-count) + AppNetworkProvider (NetworkStatsManager: per-app bytes), both gated on the PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS special-access already granted for the Battery & Usage screen. Sibling to libs:battery (the 'battery-manager', per-app energy). Providers return ranked package-name lists; app/apps maps them onto the launchable-app set for the Phone smart folders (Recent / Active 48h / Most Opened / Most Network) and the Phone 'Active Apps' section. Every query runCatching→empty so a missing grant just hides the folder.

libs:launcher-onehand.comment: One-Hand edge-gesture overlay (Samsung One Hand Operation+ style). A foreground EdgeOverlayService draws a thin near-invisible handle on the configured screen edge (WindowManager TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY) and turns swipes into global actions (Back/Home/Recents/Notifications/QuickSettings) performed by OneHandAccessibilityService. Two user-granted special perms (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW + Accessibility) — OneHandController does the deep-linking + start/stop; app/ (Configs/Onehand) is just the toggle. Fully data-driven from build.json::onehand (edge, handle size, gesture→action map baked to BuildConfig.ONEHAND_CONFIG_B64). PURE SwipeClassifier is JVM-tested. Home also has THREE stars atop this module: Sirius (SiriusStar, full circular-menu), Canopus (CanopusStar, arc-menu over Configs), and Centauri (CentaurusStar, SAME arc-menu, content = last 9 recently-opened Android apps via libs:datamanager's AppUsageProvider). ALL THREE star widget classes now live HERE (moved from app/launcher on request — 'ALL STARS in one-hand'), because ArcMenu/CircularMenu already define the app-agnostic Host boundary. Centauri needs no app callback at all (recent-apps + app icons + launch are pure platform APIs), so it takes no Host. Sirius/Canopus's CONTENT is still app-specific (Sections/SectionPages/CircularMenuTree), so THOSE classes take a Host (+ a twinkleEnabled callback for Sirius) injected from MainActivity, which builds it from its own app-side classes — the star mechanics (glyph, size, touch-forwarding, position, visibility) are generic and lib-side; only the content adapters stay in MainActivity.

libs:launcher-zoomies.comment: Zoomies pets — the animated status-bar companion. PetStrengthView (an AppCompatImageView) plays a per-tool animal whose gait (idle→walk→walk_fast→run) tracks the tool's strength, decoded from the vendored zoomies GIFs at assets/zoomies/<animal>/<variant>_<gait>.gif (CC BY-ND, used unmodified). Pure view module: no build.json config, no inter-lib deps — only androidx.appcompat. Consumed by app/launcher (LauncherStatusStrip instantiates one PetStrengthView per tool).

libs:webserver.comment: Static HTTP serving ENGINE — WebServer (one accept thread + a worker pool over java.net.ServerSocket), WebServerPrefs (port, document root, loopback-vs-LAN bind, directory listing) and the CloudWebServer process-wide singleton. Deliberately dependency-free (not even libs:core) so the planned standalone Cloud WebServer APK can take this module alone. Serves a document root with MIME typing, index.html, directory listings, a path-traversal containment check against the canonical root, and a built-in /__status JSON endpoint; a bind failure is recorded as lastError instead of thrown, because a listener that failed to bind and one that is merely idle must never look alike on a status screen. Driven by app/devcontrol's Configs > About > WEBSERVER section, which owns every label and button — the screen belongs to the app, the socket belongs here.

onehand._doc: One-Hand edge-gesture config for libs:launcher-onehand (One Hand Operation+ style), baked into BuildConfig.ONEHAND_CONFIG_B64 by libs/launcher-onehand/build.gradle and decoded by OneHandConfig. `handles[]` = one gesture pad per screen edge. Each handle: edge (left|right|bottom), position_pct (center offset along the edge), length_pct (pad length), thickness_dp (pad width), transparency (0=invisible..100=solid debug tint), edge_inset_dp (how far INSIDE the border the pad sits, leaving the very edge free for Samsung/Termux system gestures), and a `gestures` map. You activate the pad anywhere along it, then the TILT of the inward swipe picks one of seven sectors on left/right edges: `top_outer`|`top`|`top_middle`|`center`|`down_middle`|`down`|`down_outer` (center=straight inward). Bottom edge → `left`|`center`|`right` (3 sectors). A sector with no key in `gestures` safely no-ops (missing-key lookup returns null). Values are actions: none|back|home|recents|notifications|quick_settings|power_dialog|split_screen|lock_screen|screenshot|dismiss_shade|all_apps (API-gated ones no-op on old Android) OR `app:<package>` to launch an app OR `action:<target>` to open a destination INSIDE this app (`action:open_search`, `section:cloud`, a page target, a URL). The action: form wakes the app with the target in the `shortcut_action` extra, the same door the launcher long-press shortcuts use, so an edge gesture reaches exactly the surface the radial star reaches — the pickable list is circular_menu.actions, declared once and offered by both menus. Remap anything with a one-line JSON edit or in the in-app editor — never a Kotlin change (Pillar: DATA-DRIVEN).

circular_menu._doc: Sirius-star radial pie — the libs:launcher-onehand 'circular-menu', sibling to the edge-menu. Tapping the home star opens a ring of these nodes; a center arrow follows the finger, the pointed node highlights, and dragging past its ring DESCENDS into that node's children (which recenter and fan out again); releasing on a leaf navigates. Descent is RECURSIVE and arbitrary-depth: a node's `section` is its childKey — the app injects navigate(target) + iconBitmap(name) + childrenOf(key) (see app CircularMenuTree) so the lib stays app-agnostic and the tree mirrors the live sections. Example: Suite → {Cloud, Phone} → (Phone) {Home, More}; Comms/Infos → {Apps, Admin}; Labs/Configs → their pages. A node with `section:null` (Home Apps) is terminal. Star + nodes are data-driven — remap with a one-line edit, never Kotlin. TWO SEMI-CIRCLES: every level fans out as an UPWARD HALF-MOON (180° left → 270° up → 360° right) so nothing is ever drawn below the star or off the screen; radii are clamped to the viewport and derived only from the item count, so a level lays out identically every press. A descended level draws its pages on the OUTER arc (radius_dp, grown to fit the count) and its ACTIONS on a second, smaller arc ring_gap_dp below it. A child is an action when its target fires-and-returns instead of opening a page — i.e. it starts with `action:` or `extapp:` (see app CircularMenuTree.isAction), so the split is derived and no page needs a flag. A node may also declare its own `actions[]` here: extra inner-ring entries merged in on descent that are NOT pages of the section, so they never appear in the section grid or the Home row.

star._doc_pair_offset_x_dp: HALF the horizontal separation, in dp, of the two stars that share the midway row: Centauri sits this far LEFT of centre and Recent Tabs the same distance RIGHT, so one number keeps the pair symmetric about the screen's vertical axis and no star can drift into the other by an edit that forgets its twin. Sirius and Canopus stay centred (offset 0) because nothing shares their row. The floor is set by TOUCH, not by looks: each star's tap box is its glyph plus tap_pad_dp on every side, about 22 + 24 + 24 = 70dp wide, so a separation below 70dp centre-to-centre gives the two stars overlapping tap targets and the wrong menu opens. 40 leaves 80dp centre-to-centre — a 10dp clear gap — and still fits the narrowest phone this app supports (a 320dp-wide screen puts the outer edge of the right star at 235dp, well inside the viewport). dp, so the separation is the same physical distance on every density.

circular_menu._doc_actions: Root inner ring of the ALL-APPS (Sirius) star. Drawn the way every other star draws its inner ring: text only, on a smaller disc, with no icon lookup at all - so these carry no "icon" key. Targets go through the normal tile dispatcher, which is why plain https, intent:// and app:// URIs all work here with no Kotlin change.

actions._doc: Opens the DCIM/Screenshots folder directly (DocumentsUI tree URI — vendor-neutral, no root). Was 'Gallery'→gallery; the full gallery keeps its own Data Apps tile.
actions.label: Screenshots

actions._doc: App Tabs — the last-6 LRU shelf, MOVED here from Tools Primary (user request 2026-08-31). target=page:apptabs/grid lands STRAIGHT on AppTabsFragment with no page-menu intermediate, and it is opened via pushContent, so the Back arrow returns directly to the screen it was invoked from — never a nested submenu.
actions.label: Tabs

actions._doc: Added 2026-09-10 with the edge-menu reorder, because THIS list is what the one-hand action picker offers (OneHandFragment.buildOptions reads circular_menu.actions and nothing else). The left handle's `down` sector defaults to Drive; with no entry here the picker had no option matching that string, so the spinner fell back to index 0 and displayed a working slot as 'None' — one careless tap away from persisting None over it. The two strings must therefore stay identical: task 302/304 retargeted both from action:section:drive to app:com.diegonmarcos.clouddrive when Drive stopped being a section and became its own APK. The side effect is that Drive also joins the Sirius star's inner ring, which is the contract this file already states: one list, offered by both menus.
actions.label: Drive

circular_menu._doc_nodes: Outer ring of the ALL-APPS (Sirius) star: the LEAF pages, not the five parent sections. No "section" key on any of them, so CircularMenu leaves childKey null and a tap navigates straight to the target instead of descending a level. Configs is deliberately absent - it has its own star (Canopus/arc_menu).

defaults._doc_gesture_inset: The handle is inset from the very border for TWO reasons on Samsung: (1) CURVED-EDGE display — the border pixels are on the curve, where touch is unreliable (edge/palm rejection) + reserved by the system, so a handle AT the edge never activates. (2) GESTURE-nav back-swipe fires from the edge and races our press. Both are dodged by placing the handle on the FLAT glass past the curve. edge_inset_dp (26) applies always (covers the curve); edge_inset_gesture_dp (30) is used in gesture-nav (curve + a bit more to clear the back-gesture strip), detected via config_navBarInteractionMode. Flat-screen devices can lower edge_inset_dp toward 0.
defaults._doc_geometry: BOUNDED band, not full-height. length_dp=180 (>0 overrides length_pct) keeps the touch zone a ~180dp band at position_pct down the edge. Two reasons it must be bounded: (1) our handle CONSUMES touches in its area (a touchable overlay can't pass them through), so a full-height strip creates a dead vertical band down the whole edge that blocks the app underneath (e.g. Bitwarden buttons near the edge stop responding). A short band frees the rest of the edge. (2) systemGestureExclusionRects is OS-capped at 200dp/edge, so ≤180dp is FULLY excluded → reliable. Invisible (transparency 0); it lives at a consistent thumb-zone position.

handles._doc_order: THE OWNER'S SECOND BLOCK, 2026-09-10: Brave / Me / Gallery / Camera / Translator Google / Google Maps, read top to bottom. Six names for seven sectors because `center` is not one of them: a straight-in swipe was Back on BOTH handles, and Back is gone (it needs an Accessibility service; the edge menus run on Display-over-apps alone), so `center` is unmapped and the six travel down the remaining sectors in declared order — top_outer, top, top_middle, down_middle, down, down_outer. Gallery appears HERE and only here, as app:com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter — the cloud-gallery app, whose applicationId kept its old media-center spelling through the 2026-10 rename, so this target did not change while the picker label did. The first block's fifth entry is cloud-drive, which the owner corrected in a follow-up message after writing 'cloud gallery' by mistake. test-onehand-edge-order.sh pins both facts, because the message a future agent finds in the history is the uncorrected one.

THE OWNER'S FIRST BLOCK, 2026-09-10: AI Chat / Mail / Instagram / Whatsapp Business / Drive / Gemini, read top to bottom, over the same six non-center sectors the right handle uses. AI Chat (the hosted Claude bot) moved from down_outer (the last slot, where tasks #111 and #127 put it) to top_outer (the first) — that move is what identifies this block as the LEFT menu rather than the right one. Its target string did NOT change and must not: it is the working Telegram-bot URI documented below. Drive is app:com.diegonmarcos.clouddrive — task 302/304 lifted the SuperApp's own Drive section out into a real Android application, so there IS one to launch now, and the sector points at the package rather than at a section that no longer exists. The gallery remains the right handle's business.
handles._doc_top_outer: top_outer is AI (id ai-chat, formerly the Inboxes tile 'AI Claude' / ai-tlg-claude) — the same Telegram-bot target the Cloud > Apps > AGI tile uses (moved there 2026-10-14, right after Search) (@Cloud_agent_claude_bot). GestureAction.parse only understands app:/action:/bare-OneHandAction, so the intent:// URL has to travel as an action: payload: parse strips the action: prefix, openInHost forwards the rest verbatim in the shortcut_action extra, and ShellActivity's tile grammar recognises the intent: prefix and hands it to Intent.parseUri. Keep the two targets identical — if the bot handle changes, change it here as well. NOTE: search left this handle in the same commit that reordered it — top_outer used to be action:open_search, which is now the Polaris star at the top of the home screen (onehand.search_star).

onehand._doc_retired_targets: #537 (third report of the same Drive defect, after #404 and #284). A sector's DEFAULT lives in handles[], but an override the owner once picked lives in OneHandPrefs on the phone and BEATS the default forever. The left `down` default was action:section:drive from 2026-09-10 until #302/#304 lifted Drive into its own APK on 2026-09-13; any override written in that window still names a section that no longer exists, so the edge drew a title-cased raw target with no glyph and the tap opened nothing — while every tester, all reading handles[], stayed green. This map is old target -> its successor, applied by OneHandConfig.effective() to STORED overrides only, so a destination that was retired is followed to where it moved instead of pinning the phone to a dead one. It never touches a live choice: only a key listed here is rewritten. Keys are written exactly as OneHandPrefs stores a value (GestureAction.serialize(): `action:<target>`, `app:<pkg>`, or a bare global id). Add a row whenever a sector target is retired.
onehand._doc_search_star: POLARIS — the home screen's fifth star, asked for on 2026-09-10: 'Search (cloud-superapp) should become a new star in the launcher/one-hand, add it on the top of the screen'. It opens the SuperApp's OWN search, the SearchSheet that ShellActivity.openSearchSheet already shows for the top-bar magnifier and for action:open_search; nothing new was invented for it. Glyph, size and tap padding come from circular_menu.star, so all five stars stay one size. WHY IT CARRIES A SINGLE `target` AND NOT AN `actions[]` LIST LIKE ITS SIBLINGS: every other star opens a menu that fans UPWARD, and ArcMenu caps its radius at min(cx, width - cx, cy - topInset) - margin. At the top of the screen cy - topInset is NEGATIVE, that cap collapses to its floor, and the menu draws off the top edge. A star up here can only be a single destination, so a list would be flexibility that cannot be used. Change what it opens by changing `target` — any string the tile dispatcher understands. top_offset_dp is measured from the top of the screen to the TOP of the star's touch box, and its floor is the top island: toolbar_island sits at layout_marginTop 26dp and is one ?attr/actionBarSize (56dp on a phone) tall, so anything at or below 82dp clears it. 92 leaves 10dp. Nothing else lives up here — Sirius is centred, Centauri and Recent Tabs share the midway row, Canopus sits above the bottom island — so this star displaces none of them.
onehand._doc_apps: App vocabulary offered in the per-swipe action picker (OneHandFragment). Each entry launches its package via getLaunchIntentForPackage; a package the phone doesn't have is silently skipped at fire time. Add an app = one entry — no Kotlin change.

apps._doc_fleet: The four fleet apps the reordered handles now default to, added 2026-09-10 so the picker shows them under their real names at the top of the list instead of leaving the owner to find them among every installed app. Packages are quoted from ui.external_apps, which is where this repository keeps app identity — cloud-mail is com.diegonmarcos.comms.mail (the applicationId did NOT move when it became a Sterna clone), and cloud-camera is cld.camera, our renamed GrapheneOS Camera build. Obsidian and Bitwarden stay in this list although they are no longer defaults: a favourite is what you can pick, not what you get.
apps.label: cloud-mail

apps._doc: Added when the Drive surface left the SuperApp and became its own APK (#302/#304). The left handle's down gesture used to be `action:section:drive`; there is no drive section any more, so the gesture now launches the application — and a gesture may only name a package this picker offers, which is why the entry has to exist here and not only in the handle.
apps.label: cloud-drive

onehand._doc_radial: Two-finger radial menu (libs:launcher-onehand, UNWIRED: it needed the accessibility service's onMotionEvent, which the edge menus no longer use). Hold TWO fingers anywhere ~still for two_finger_hold_ms → a ring of icons opens at that point; release to one finger and move it to the icon (arrow follows), lift to fire. Because it only observes touches, the app underneath also sees the fingers (may pinch) — that's the cost of not intercepting. items[] are actions: `app:<pkg>` (global action ids such as back|home|recents are no longer supported). radius_dp = ring radius; slop_dp = how far the 2-finger centroid may drift before the hold cancels.

radial._doc_security: enabled=false by DEFAULT on purpose: the radial menu works by OBSERVING ALL touches system-wide (FLAG_SEND_MOTION_EVENTS), which is a genuine privacy/security capability — it can see taps anywhere, including over a password manager. Turn it on ONLY as a conscious opt-in. While disabled, the service never requests motion-event observation at all.

arc_menu._doc_actions: Deliberately empty. KDE Connect and Animations moved into ui.sections[config].pages as is_action entries, which feed the arc's inner ring AND the Configs grid from one list. The block stays because it is still the right home for an action that belongs on the STAR only - one that would be noise in the grid.

onehand._doc_recents_menu: Inner ring of the Centauri star (outer ring = RECENT APPS, last-9-opened): what you do TO the recent apps, as opposed to the outer ring which launches them. Dispatched by CentaurusStar.recentsAction. Android gives a non-system launcher no way to clear another app's Overview card, so close_all/kill_bg kill BACKGROUND processes (only cached ones die; the cards remain either way — both toast an attempt count so the action is never a silent no-op) (an 'Active Apps' entry that opened the system Overview needed Accessibility and was removed).
onehand._doc_home_swipes: Configurable home-screen gestures, all editable live in Configs > Launcher > One-Hand. Swipes (fire on the Home root only): swipe_up opens Cloud > Apps; swipe_down_left (a swipe down that STARTS on the left half of the screen) opens Notify; swipe_down_right (starts on the right half) opens Quick Actions (page:config/controls); swipe_left opens the last Cloud app launched (open_last_cloud_app: the newest launched app that is a fleet/constellation app, else Cloud > Apps); swipe_right opens the last SuperApp page (open_last_superapp_page). Any `page:<section>/<page>` target works, no code edit. Other named actions: open_last_android_app | walk_step_next | walk_step_prev | toggle_light (libs:light, flips the default light) | open_cloud_calc. The old Home Apps sheet is gone: the legacy ids open_home_apps / open_home_apps_phone route to page:cloud/apps / page:phone/apps. Shapes: a stroke at least shape_gestures.min_length_dp long whose end-to-start distance is under max_straightness of its length is a drawn SHAPE, not a swipe: it goes to the recogniser (launcher/ShapeRecogniser.kt) and never to the swipe detector, so the two cannot conflict. The recogniser resamples the stroke to `resample` points, scales it to a unit box, centres it, tries each of rotations_deg and compares it with every template below by the mean two-way nearest-point distance; the best template wins when its distance is at most max_distance and beats the runner-up by min_margin. Size is free, rotation is tolerated within rotations_deg, start point and direction are free. Templates are DATA: `points` are x,y pairs (y down) of the ideal stroke; add a gesture here (id, label, action, points) and it is recognised with no Kotlin. A short trail is drawn under the finger while a curved stroke is in progress.

home_status_bar._doc: THE HOME STATUS BAR, DECLARED (Configs > Launcher > One-Hand > Status Bar). The top row of the home screen, drawn by launcher/LauncherStatusStrip.kt, RENDERS FROM THIS LIST: each element is placed in the cluster named by `position` (left | centre | right), in `order`, and only when `visible`; moving an element, changing its order or hiding it here changes the bar and nothing else has to be edited. `kind` picks the drawing (network = label over four signal dots, clock = the date and time, metric = a load figure, battery = the battery icon); `id` of a network element is the NetworkSections key, so the tap target stays the popup section of the same name; `short` is the caption drawn on the bar (the web replica uses it as is; the phone's mobile caption is live, 5G | Call | SOS); `pet` is the Zoomies animal row above it (status_pets), null for none; `opens` is what a tap does (network_popup | system_popup | battery_popup | tasks_popup). The clock's `format` is a SimpleDateFormat pattern. The Status Bar section of the One-Hand page lists these elements and stores the owner's runtime overrides (a visibility switch per element, an order per cluster) in status_bar_prefs; the declaration is the default. `row_height_dp` is the 26 dp the strip leaves above the toolbar island (res/values/dimens.xml::shell_top_row_margin; test-status-bar-declared.sh holds them equal). `toolbar_row` lists, read-only, the two pills of the toolbar island drawn right under the strip: they are not strip elements and the strip does not render them.

toolbar_row.label: Music pill (now playing)
toolbar_row.source: ShellActivity: the first pill of the toolbar island; its target is the package that owns the live media session, discovered at runtime

tasks_popup._doc: THE TASKS POPUP (was 'Agenda | Calendar'): what the status bar's clock opens (home_status_bar.elements[clock].opens = tasks_popup). cal/TasksPopup.kt reads this block (BuildConfig.TASKS_POPUP_B64) for its title, its default view, the number of months and every size. `label` is the one name, also the string tasks_label in values and values-es. `default_view` is the view it opens on (calendar | agenda). `views`: calendar = the months on top with the Agenda and Todo tables under them; agenda = the two tables alone, in the larger table height. `months`: previous, current and next, stacked, so count = before + 1 + after (the parser refuses anything else); today is a filled disc and a day with an event carries a dot. Tapping a day filters the Agenda table to that day, tapping it again clears the filter. `tables`: agenda = upcoming dated items (date, time, title) from the cal ENGINE's events (Cloud-Lib-Cal.apk, build.json::engines.cal, the same one Cloud Tasks and Cloud Me read); todo = the open items of the engine's VTODO mirror (the same one Cloud Tasks writes). `complete` is false for todo: completing a task writes to the CalDAV server and the engine takes the account from the app that owns the credentials (Cloud Tasks), which this app does not hold, so the checkbox is drawn but disabled and a tap on the row opens Cloud Tasks. Sizes are dp.
tasks_popup.label: Tasks

onehand_page._doc: THE INDEX OF Configs > Launcher > One-Hand: a sticky row of icon anchors at the top of the page, one per section, in the page's order; a tap scrolls to that section. OneHandFragment draws the sections AND the index from this one list (BuildConfig.ONEHAND_PAGE_B64), so an anchor cannot point at a section the page does not have, nor a section lack an anchor (test-onehand-index.sh). `label` is the anchor caption, `heading` the section heading on the page, `icon` a name of the libs:ui-icons catalog (the only icons a declaration may name).

_doc_wifi_analyzer: #1263 the WiFi page's host config, baked into BuildConfig.WIFI_ANALYZER_B64 and deep-merged by libs:wifi over its assets/wifi/wifi-config.json (any key of that file may be overridden here). throughput = the endpoint Tools > Throughput downloads from / uploads to ({bytes} becomes the byte budget); ping.default_host = the public host of the latency test; scan = the auto-scan interval and Android's foreground throttle (4 scans / 2 min); rssi = the signal thresholds the page colours by.

privileged_channel._default_on_doc: Whether this app arms the privileged channel by itself (auto-connect at start/boot, Wireless debugging re-arm, a privileged tool's implicit reconnect). SuperApp: OFF until the user enables Configs > Keep Wireless debugging on (must equal that control's default_on; test-channel-auto-arm.sh). Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools ChannelAutoArm from the same baked block.
privileged_channel._doc: What THIS app declares it needs the privileged shell channel for. Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle into BuildConfig.CHANNEL_NEEDS_B64 and listed, as written, in the Declared needs section of the ADB Shell page (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools AdbShellPage). Add a need here and it shows there; nothing about it is typed in Kotlin. Each need: id (unique), label, why (one sentence), commands (the shell verbs it runs).

needs.why: Runs the shizuku_diagnostics bundles: dumpsys battery and usb, sysfs power-supply reads.

needs.why: The Installs block toggles the verifier settings.

shizuku_diagnostics._doc: Data-driven catalog of shell-domain diagnostic bundles run by libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools. Two execution channels share this catalog (ladder, first ready wins): (1) local_server — OUR OWN app_process server (AdbShellServer) started once per boot via the adb one-liner from /api/adb/server-command; it runs in the SHELL SELinux domain (uid 2000) so dumpsys/usb/sysfs that untrusted_app is denied all work. NO third-party app. (2) Shizuku UserService — optional fallback when its app happens to be running. The lib's build.gradle base64-encodes bundles[] into BuildConfig.ADB_DIAG_BUNDLES_B64; AdbDiagnostics decodes + runs the chosen bundle, returning {bundle,label,channel,ok,results:[{id,cmd,out}]}. Adding a diagnostic = one entry here, no Kotlin edit (Pillar: DATA-DRIVEN). READ-ONLY diagnostics only — never a write/mutation.

local_server._doc: OUR app_process shell-domain server. Started by `adb shell CLASSPATH=<apk> app_process /system/bin <class> <token> <port>` (the /api/adb/server-command one-liner, run once per boot via wireless debugging). Loopback + per-boot random token. This is the self-contained replacement for the Shizuku app.

commands.cmd: for d in /sys/class/power_supply/*; do echo "== ${d##*/} =="; for f in type online present status charge_type usb_type voltage_now current_now current_max voltage_max input_current_limit constant_charge_current_max power_now temp; do v=$(cat "$d/$f" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$f=$v"; done; done
for d in /sys/class/typec/port*; do echo "== ${d##*/} =="; for f in power_role data_role vconn_source power_operation_mode; do v=$(cat "$d/$f" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$f=$v"; done; done
for f in /sys/class/android_usb/android0/state /sys/class/udc/*/state; do echo "$f=$(cat $f 2>/dev/null)"; done
for z in /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*; do t=$(cat "$z/type" 2>/dev/null); v=$(cat "$z/temp" 2>/dev/null); echo "$t=$v"; done
for d in /sys/class/typec/*; do echo "== $d =="; grep -sr . "$d" 2>/dev/null | sed 's#/sys/class/typec/##'; done

samsung_sfc._doc: Data-driven inputs for the SfcVerdict parser (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools/SfcVerdict.kt), baked into BuildConfig.SFC_CONFIG_B64 by this module's build.gradle. The parser is PURE / JVM-testable and reads NO hardcoded device data — the model->max-watts ceiling map lives here so a new Galaxy model is a one-line JSON edit, never a Kotlin change. `device_caps` is keyed by model-number PREFIX (parser matches the longest startsWith of `ro.product.model`); value = the device's MAXIMUM wired watts (a higher-rated cable/charger cannot exceed it). `high_voltage_mv_threshold` = the dumpsys mcv / Max-charging-voltage (mV) at/above which a high-voltage fast-charge contract is considered engaged (9V = 9000). `full_level_pct` = SOC at/above which fast charge tapers, so a 'not negotiating' verdict is expected, not a fault.

status_pets._doc: Status-bar Line 0 animated pets (vendored from github.com/KartikLabhshetwar/zoomies, sprites CC BY-ND 4.0 — used UNMODIFIED + credited). Each Line-1 tool gets a FIXED animal above it; the tool's strength maps to a gait level 0..3 = idle/walk/walk_fast/run (the animal stays, the gait speeds up). Fully data-driven: sync-zoomies vendors exactly the animal/variant GIFs referenced here; app/build.gradle bakes this block to BuildConfig.STATUS_PETS_B64; LauncherStatusStrip renders + drives it.

adb._doc: ADB icon (USB or Wireless debugging on). Reuses an already-vendored sprite pair, so sync-zoomies copies nothing new.

usb._doc: The Data icon (USB-C cable in a data mode or OTG host); keeps the id the old USB icon had, so its pet is unchanged.

hotspot._doc: HS icon (Wi-Fi hotspot / USB / Bluetooth tethering). Reuses an already-vendored sprite pair.

voice._doc: Offline voice-input (Vosk) model registry for libs:voice, behind the keyboard VOICE toolbar key. libs/voice/build.gradle bakes this into BuildConfig.VOICE_MODELS_JSON + VOICE_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE; VoiceModelManager downloads the model for the active keyboard language lazily on first use, unzips to filesDir/vosk/<dir>, then Vosk runs fully offline (no Google/system speech IME). Add a language = one entry. Small models keep each download ~40-50MB.

keyboard_dicts._doc: Bundled keyboard dictionaries → libs/keyboard/dicts-data/ (read by DictionaryInfoUtils.ASSETS_DICTIONARY_FOLDER). The keyboard tree already ships main_<locale>.dict for these locales (word suggestions); sync-keyboard-dicts ADDS the matching emoji_<locale>.dict (emoji search) from codeberg.org/Helium314/aosp-dictionaries (GPL-3.0) so each supported language has FULL features. Additive copy (no --delete). Locales/types data-driven — add a locale or a type (with its repo dir) = one entry. NOTE: `locales` = which dicts are BUNDLED (broad, for any language the user adds); `default_languages` = which keyboard subtypes are ENABLED on first run (App.initVendoredKeyboard via SubtypeSettings.addEnabledSubtype) — distinct lists.

keyboard_media._doc: Data-driven config for the keyboard Sticker/GIF panel (libs:media, hosted in the emoji surface by patch 0007). Non-secret ONLY — GIF provider API keys are secrets: build.sh sops-decrypts .keyboard_media.vault_secrets from the vault and exports TENOR_API_KEY/GIPHY_API_KEY into the gradle build (app/build.gradle → BuildConfig → MediaRuntime.configure). Whole block is shipped to the APK as base64 (BuildConfig.MEDIA_CONFIG_B64). Switch the GIF backend by changing gif.provider (tenor|giphy) — both are pre-configured so you flip without touching code. Row-2 GIF categories = gif.<provider>.categories; a category query "" means the provider's trending/featured feed. Stickers have no categories here — one row-2 tab per installed WhatsApp-compatible pack is discovered at runtime.

_doc_fleet_agents: THE AGENT REGISTRY (Configs ▸ Fleet ▸ Agents). Every fleet app declares the agents it runs here, top level, in this ONE shape: {id, name, kind, trigger, open, status, summary}. kind is one of on-device worker | on-device service | agent door | in-app agent | remote gateway agent | bound engine. trigger says what starts it (a schedule or an event). open is where its page is: a page: target of the declaring app, which the consolidator turns into extapp:<app>#page:... for every app but this one. status names the LOCAL channel live status is read through: workmanager (unique work name), workmanager_tag, service (a service class of this app), provider (a fleet app's own read-only provider: authority_suffix + path, one row), provider_presence (the provider is there or not), installed (a fleet row's package), or none with the reason it is not exposed yet. No status source is ever an HTTP call between apps. A row may instead be {from, path, ...defaults}: one row per item of a list declared elsewhere (Cloud Search's agents catalogue, the shared agents.json), so a list is never restated. 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-agents.py consolidates every app's block into data/fleet-agents.json (regen.sh runs it; fleet-agents-guard.yml fails when the file is stale).
