engines._doc: #713 ENGINES THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING — same contract as ac_cloud-drive/build.json::engines (#705): `fleet` is the Store row in data/constellation-fleet.json whose package app/build.gradle resolves (an unknown id fails the build), `action` finds the engine service in it, `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT that answers every method profile/GhEngine.kt calls (read through PackageManager before any bind), `login_poll_ms` / `login_max_ms` pace gh's device-flow sign-in, which the engine runs on its own thread and the client polls. The Account page's GitHub ▸ WebAuth is this engine's `gh auth login` — GitHub CLI's own public client inside gh, never an OAuth app of the fleet's. 1_cicd engine-contract-guard holds every app's client to the engine it binds.

feed._doc: engine-apk-split move 4: the RSS pane (rss/RemoteFeed.kt) binds Cloud-Lib-Feed.apk; libs:feed is in no module map here, so a feed change republishes that APK and not this app.

cal._doc: The Tasks popup (cal/TasksFeed.kt) binds Cloud-Lib-Cal.apk for its Agenda (events) and Todo (todos) tables, the engine Cloud Tasks and Cloud Me already read; libs:cal is in no module map here. min_contract 1 answers events and todos.

ui._doc_permissions: Data-driven master list for Configs/About → Permissions. `runtime` = standard runtime-grantable Android perms (Android 6+ dangerous perms — Camera/Mic/Location/Contacts/etc.). DevControlFragment reads this list, renders one row per entry with live grant state, and bulk-requests the union via ActivityResultContracts.RequestMultiplePermissions. Special-access perms (battery whitelist, default launcher, usage stats), Health Connect perms, and System auto-granted perms are computed AT RUNTIME inside DevControlFragment — they don't need a JSON list because they're either single-flag toggles or PackageManager-introspected sets.

permissions._doc_device: #632 DEVICE-STATE rows: things the setup checklist must get DONE and CHECKED that are not an Android permission at all, so neither a runtime dialog nor a special-access page can express them. Play Protect is the first and the reason the group exists: the fleet sideloads every app (#571 WE ARE THE STORE) and GmsCore's package verifier warns on, delays or silently flags a sideloaded APK — a plausible contributor to #200 (Collabora installs silently with no error) and #163 (install stuck in downloading). Each row names a `key` the page maps to a REAL system read (never a remembered flag, the #622/#452 rule) plus the remedy text and, where we cannot flip it ourselves, where the user can. THE APP CANNOT TURN PLAY PROTECT OFF: the three Settings.Global values behind it need WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, a signature permission no sideloaded APK holds, so the row deep-links to the toggle and states the remedy rather than pretending. The privileged path exists and is NOT depended on here: with the embedded adb channel paired (#280/#281) `settings put global package_verifier_user_consent -1` sets it directly, which is what the Play Protect button in the Installs block already does through PackageVerifier.setScanning. READING is unprivileged, but Settings.Global.getInt(key, default) cannot tell an ABSENT key from a stock value — so the row verifies the key is actually stored and says it cannot verify when it is not, rather than showing a tick it cannot justify.

device.label: Play Protect install scan OFF
device.remedy: Play Store → profile → Play Protect → Settings → turn off "Scan apps with Play Protect"

permissions._doc_special: Special permissions the SuperApp itself needs and Android never shows a runtime dialog for. Rendered at the top of Configs > Permissions > OPEN A SYSTEM PAGE and asked, in this order, by the first-run step (system/FirstRunPerms.kt; Skip, and never again after 2 skips). INSTALL_UNKNOWN = PackageManager.canRequestPackageInstalls(), granted on Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES (package-scoped) - the SuperApp installs the fleet. HOME = RoleManager.isRoleHeld(ROLE_HOME) on API 29+ (resolveActivity CATEGORY_HOME below), requested with RoleManager.createRequestRoleIntent(ROLE_HOME), falling back to Settings.ACTION_HOME_SETTINGS. Both re-checked on resume. Kept in step with system/SpecialPerms.kt by SpecialPermsTest.
permissions._doc_roles: Single-holder RoleManager roles surfaced as Special-access rows on Configs/About → Permissions. These are NOT held by the SuperApp (it's a launcher with no dialer / call-screening service) — the holder is the Cloud-Comms phone fork (or Fossify Phone in the interim). The SuperApp cannot grant another app a role programmatically (createRequestRoleIntent only ever targets the calling app), so each row (a) reads the LIVE holder via RoleManager.getRoleHolders / TelecomManager.getDefaultDialerPackage and shows ✓ when the holder is one of `expected_holders`, and (b) the 'Set Default Apps' button deep-links to Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_DEFAULT_APPS_SETTINGS so the user picks Cloud-Comms there. `role` is the literal android.app.role.* constant passed straight to RoleManager. When our own fork ships, add its package to the relevant expected_holders[] — zero code change.
permissions._doc_privileged: Signature/privileged perms Android will NEVER show a runtime dialog for. They are grantable only by the shell user (uid 2000) via `pm grant <pkg> <perm>` over the privileged plane (embedded adb / Shizuku / cloud-superapp-mcp superapp_grant). A `pm grant` persists across reboots AND across in-place updates of the same package (silent installs are updates, not reinstalls), so one grant is for all time until an uninstall. READ_LOGS is what lets an app read the FULL system logcat into its own log view instead of only its own uid — the Registros/Logs screen needs it to be useful. `apps` is an OPTIONAL override: when present it is the exact list granted (used to NARROW a grant, e.g. WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS goes to superapp only). When absent, PrivilegedPlaneWorker resolves targets dynamically as fleet ∩ installed packages whose own manifest declares that permission — `pm grant` is a silent no-op for a package that never declared the perm. READ_LOGS is narrowed back to the superapp DELIBERATELY, and the earlier note here claiming the dynamic list rescued nix-on-droid and termux from 'the logcat dialog forever' had the causality backwards: holding READ_LOGS is what SENDS an app to that dialog. It maps the process into the `log` supplementary gid (frameworks/base data/etc/platform.xml), and that gid is precisely the test logd applies in clientHasLogCredentials() — a client without it is served its own uid's lines immediately and silently (system/logging/logd/LogReader.cpp:260), while a client WITH it is routed to LogcatManagerService's SystemUI consent dialog. That consent cannot be persisted by any means: it lives in an in-memory map cleared 60s after each approval, there is no app-op behind it, and the dialog has no 'remember' control. So granting it fleet-wide to stop the prompts made every app prompt instead. Only the superapp's cross-app log viewer genuinely needs it; every other fleet reader is written for own-uid output already.

privileged.label: Write secure settings (re-enable Wireless Debugging on boot)
Dump system services (dumpsys from the ADB Shell page and the fleet API, Shizuku stopped)

privileged._doc: #736 the terminals bind ~/emulated and ~/cloud-shared-store only when /storage/emulated/0 is readable, and a fresh install has no storage grant. Both target SDK 28, where the legacy READ/WRITE runtime pair is what opens shared storage (All-Files-Access is ignored below target 30). Each terminal asks for it itself at every session start; this entry lets the plane grant it with no prompt once embedded adb is armed. Runtime permissions are not development-flagged, so they reach a package only through an explicit apps list, and staleGrants never revokes them (a user may have granted them through the dialog). Every package here must be a constellation-fleet package whose manifest declares the permission: aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-terminal-storage-grant.sh.
privileged.label: Shared storage for the terminals (read ~/emulated, ~/cloud-shared-store)

ui._doc: Navigation taxonomy - data-driven source for MainActivity's BottomNavigationView (bottom buttons), DrawerLayout (left-side collapsable 2-level menu), and per-section Toolbar menus. Every section child is a PAGE: one `pages` list per section feeds the section grid, the bottom-nav long-press fan, the Sirius ring and the tablet detail pane. The retired `tab:` and `mode:` target prefixes and the per-section `long_press` list were all just 'open child X of section Y' - write `page:<section>/<page>`. Adding a new section = one entry here + one drawable + one fragment placeholder.
ui._doc_bottom_nav: The bottom-nav island (libs:bottomnav, #531): the sections it shows, left to right. THE one declaration of which sections are in the bar and in what order - Home in the centre. It replaced res/menu/bottom_nav.xml (the order and ids) AND the per-section bottom_nav booleans (membership), which were two declarations of one list. Each entry is a ui.sections id; its label and per-mode icon come from that section. A section not listed here is reached from the drawer or a tile. ShellBottomNav reads it through BuildConfig.UI_BOTTOM_NAV; five fit the island's even cells at phone width.
ui._doc_home_index: The `home` section is the master index — its content is a TileGrid of every other section. Lives at the center of the bottom nav (replacing Chat, which moves to drawer-only). Tapping any drawer tab or bottom-nav button always lands the right-pane on that section's TileGrid (sub-pages as squared tiles).
ui._doc_aggregator_sections: Aggregator sections are pure NAV — their tiles deep-link into real content sections via target ids ('section:X' | 'page:X/Y' | 'action:X' | 'extapp:X' | a URI). Each declares tiles_shared (section-wide) and/or a tiles_<page-id> / stack_<page-id> pair per child. Children marked "facet": true render THIS section's lists (LauncherNavController.aggregatorPage, which prefers stack_<id>, then tiles_<id>, then the section-wide tile_groups); non-facet children are ordinary pages served by a SectionPages factory — or, when they declare a `url`, by WebPageFragment. The bottom nav hosts exactly these 5 aggregators: Inboxes · Projects · HOME · Cloud · Phone.

sections.label: Notify
sections._doc_pages: Notify — one Apps RSS stack, six PRESETS of it. Every tab renders the SAME three panels (Cloud publishers, Phone apps, C3 Ntfy) and differs only in the `default` of its taxonomy rows, so a preset is data, not a second implementation: All shows everything, and the other five open pre-narrowed to one phone-taxonomy section. C3 Ntfy stopped being its own tab and became the third panel plus a Source option, because it was never a different KIND of page — only a different origin, which Source already models. Filter choices are remembered per PAGE ID, so narrowing one preset never disturbs another. Msgs moved out to Projects (page id kept, relabelled Inboxes): it is a mail/chat console, not a notification stack, and it never belonged on a page whose every sibling reads a notification store.
sections._doc_stack_my-rss: Apps RSS is a NOTIFICATION CENTRE divided per app, not a stack of feeds. It declares one card per STREAM and each card renders one group per PUBLISHER. Phone stream: the group key is the notification's own `packageName`, labelled with its `appLabel` — carried by the notification itself, so an app installed tomorrow groups correctly with no edit here and no package list to rot. Cloud stream: the group key is the ntfy TOPIC (and the `source` field for the in-app feed), because a cloud message has no package and the address it was published to is the closest thing it carries to one — a topic has exactly one publisher the way a package has exactly one app. Grouping by SCOPE was the alternative and is wrong: advisory/user/cloud is a routing category shared by many publishers, so it would collapse every unrelated channel into one bucket, which is the undivided list this page replaced. Scope still selects WHICH topics the cloud card carries, via `scopes` below, over the same ui.ntfy catalog Infra RSS browses — there is still no second topic list anywhere. The old rss / notifications / phone_notifications / news_feeds panels are gone: three of the four were child fragments embedded through the fixed host-id pool, which is exactly what cannot survive a card that re-renders on every toggle tap. EVERY panel here must declare "stream": "phone", "cloud" or "channels" — a panel that declares none renders a bare `no stream declared` line and logs the panel title to logcat, because the grammar for fixing it is addressed to whoever opens THIS file and is useless to the person holding the phone. THE TWO BADGE PANELS (#580) belong to THIS page only (stack_my-rss, the All tab — the other five do not declare them) and are not notification streams: `notification_badges` is the persistent-badge boxes (BadgePanes.badges, live state from BadgeServices) and carries `above_filters: true`, which draws it ABOVE the Filters row instead of below it; `notification_badge_configs` is the customization menus that used to be the Push tab (BadgePanes.configs), declared `collapsed` so it starts folded under the Filters. Both are VIEWS onto the badges that already live in the one notification centre and read ui.notification_center — neither posts, clears or stores anything, so the #497/#515 single-centre guards (test-notification-centre-is-singular T2/T4-T7) are untouched. Configs ▸ Launcher ▸ Notify mirrors this page, so it shows them too; they carry no `origin`, so the Source filter never hides them.
sections._doc_filters_my-rss: The five toggles above the Apps RSS stack. Declared here, not in Kotlin: the OPTION SET and the LABELS are data, only the five filter IDS (sort|source|tools|services|show) are a contract the fragment implements. `default` is what a phone shows before the user has ever touched the row; the choice is then remembered per page in SharedPreferences (committed, not applied — this app is the launcher and Android restarts it many times an hour, so a queued write is a setting that silently reverts), and a stored id this file no longer declares falls back to the default rather than stranding the row on an invisible choice. SORT now chooses the ORDER OF THE APP GROUPS — App = alphabetical, Time = most recently active app first — never whether grouping happens, because the division per app IS this page; inside a group the order is always newest-first, so flipping Sort can never bury something fresh. TIME IS THE DEFAULT ON ALL SIX TABS and it is declared HERE, never in Kotlin, so what a phone shows before anyone has touched the row is a build.json edit; test/test-notify-sort-default.sh asserts every generated tab carries the same one, because a default fixed on the tab you happened to open and missing from the other five is exactly the failure this page is shaped to produce. Sort reaches the ntfy CHANNEL boxes too: those were ordered alphabetically under BOTH modes, which made them the one construction site where Time did nothing, and since every tab draws its channels through that same code the page read as name-ordered on all six while this file said time on all six. A channel is ordered on its LAST MEASUREMENT, and one that has never been polled — or whose poll failed — sorts last rather than claiming a freshness nobody measured; the order is fixed at draw time so a poll landing can never reshuffle boxes under the reader's thumb. SOURCE works off each panel's `origin` below rather than any package list: a stream is Phone or Cloud by WHERE IT COMES FROM, which cannot go stale. SHOW is All vs Unread and NOT All vs Dismissed: neither NotificationStore nor PhoneNotificationStore records a dismissed flag — PhoneNotificationStore deliberately keeps entries the system already dismissed, and opening the cloud card calls cancelAll(), which destroys dismissal state rather than recording it, so a Dismissed filter would read a field nothing writes and render an eternally empty list. Unread needs no new field at all: it is `ts > last visit`, read before the watermark is advanced so toggling within one visit keeps answering the same question, and both stores already carry ts. TOOLS and SERVICES filter by the PHONE-APPS TAXONOMY: each option id IS the section prefix character declared in ui.phone_sections, so a section added there becomes filterable with no Kotlin change, and PhoneTaxonomy resolves a package to its prefix through the same PhoneAppClassifier + phone_folders the launcher uses. They are ONE choice spread over two rows — an app is a Tool or a Service, never both, so narrowing one row returns the other to All rather than AND-ing to a permanently empty page. They prune the phone groups before rendering, not after, so an empty result still lands on the filtered-away note. AN OPTION ID IS A SET OF PREFIXES, not one prefix: "-+" (Services) matches both Services · Buro (-) and Services · Others (+), and "=>*" (Tools) matches Primary (=), Media (>) and Health (*). AggregatorStackFragment.taxonomyKeeps tests membership, so single-character ids keep working unchanged and every phone_sections prefix stays reachable from some tab. THE SIX NOTIFY TABS are one page cloned six times: they all share stack_* (cloud + phone + C3-ntfy) and differ only in their filters_<pageid> defaults — my-rss all/all, rss-inboxes @, rss-data ., rss-tools =>*, rss-services -+, rss-sys _. Selections persist per PAGE ID, so a tab the user retunes keeps its own bucket and the others stay on their preset.
sections._doc_origin_my-rss: `origin` is the Cloud-vs-Phone classifier, and it is a property of the STREAM, not of any individual notification. Everything captured by the notification listener is by construction from an app installed on this device (phone); everything in the ntfy catalog and the in-app SuperApp feed is by construction from off-device (cloud). Each card renders the stream its own `origin` would hide, so `origin` and `stream` cannot disagree. A panel with no `origin` is never hidden by the Source toggle — an unclassified card stays visible rather than disappearing, the same fail-visible rule ui.ntfy.scopes uses for an unknown prefix.
sections._doc_scopes_my-rss: `scopes` selects WHICH ui.ntfy topics the Cloud publishers card polls; a topic whose scope is not listed is not fetched at all. An empty CHANNELS list therefore means no channel in ui.ntfy falls in this card's scopes — nothing is being polled, which is NOT the same as every channel being quiet, and the card says only "no channels in scope" because the person holding the phone cannot close a declaration gap. AggregatorStackFragment.renderNtfyGroups logs the panel and its scopes to logcat when it happens. A panel that declares no `scopes` at all carries the whole catalog rather than nothing, the same fail-visible rule `origin` uses.

sections._doc_moved_cloud: stack_cloud / tiles_cloud USED to hang here — GHA runs, repo commits and the Dagu deeplink. They are now sections[c3].stack_observability, under Cloud ▸ C3 ▸ Observability — which IS the c3 section's own Observability tab, not a copy of it beside the pages it points at. Nothing else keyed off them: `page:infos/cloud` addresses the PAGE, not these lists.
sections._doc_stack_msgs: Projects ▸ Inboxes. A card here is a CHANNEL CLASS — Mail, Chat, Messenger, RSS — and never one app. The owner asked for this on 2026-09-10: the page used to carry one card per app (Mail · accounts, Chat · Matrix, Chat · Mattermost, Messenger (Element), Dialer (Fossy)), which meant the question "is there anything for me in my messages" had to be asked five times and re-asked every time an app was installed. A panel names its class with `class: <id>`, an id from ui.inbox_classes, and draws that class's slice of the SAME phone notification feed Notify ▸ Inboxes reads, with a counted summary above it. WHY THE MEMBERSHIP IS NOT WRITTEN HERE: it lives in ui.inbox_classes beside ui.phone_folders, because a package roster is a CLASSIFICATION and every classification in this file lives under ui.* keyed on package — phone_folders, ntfy.taxon, external_apps. A roster inside a stack would be the only one that no other surface and no tester could read. WHY A FIFTH CARD: four curated classes are not a catch-all, and the card this page replaced was. An app that no class claims lands in the class marked `catch_all: true` (Other) rather than vanishing — the owner installing a messaging app nobody classified must still see its notifications on the screen they check, and a screen that silently drops notifications is worse than the per-app screen it replaced. WHAT THE SUMMARY IS: counts, measured from the notification listener — how many apps or channels the class holds, how many notifications, and how long ago the newest one arrived. It is deliberately not a written digest: kind=stats on this page prints numbers declared in this file under the caption 'Mock data — live fetch pending', and replacing five mock dashboards with a sixth, or with a paid model call the owner did not ask to pay for, would be a worse card than an honest count. WHAT MAIL REACHES: mail NOTIFICATIONS, not mail content. The message bodies live in the mail app's own store; ui.mail_accounts on this page is connection config (server, user, ports) and carries no messages, which is why renderMailAccounts has always captioned its own list 'Unread / total counts pending JMAP slice C2 + IMAP slice'. The Mail card says so on the card rather than presenting the lesser thing under the greater name. RSS is the one class that is not phone packages: it declares `source: c3ntfy` and reuses the stream=channels renderer the C3 Ntfy panel already had, so it is a retitle plus a summary and not new plumbing.

stack_msgs._doc: The unified inbox: fleet mail (cloud-mail agentmail provider, unread first) plus every app's notifications from the SuperApp's listener, grouped by app — icon, sender, preview, time; a tap opens the thread when the app left one, else the app. The class cards below stay as the per-class view.
stack_msgs.title: All inboxes
stack_msgs.subtitle: Fleet + phone apps

stack_msgs._doc: Declares extapp:cloud-matrix so the card header opens Element, the messenger the owner actually reads. The class it draws is far wider than that one app — see ui.inbox_classes[messenger] — which is the whole point of classing by channel and not by app.
stack_msgs.title: Messenger

stack_msgs._doc: No `url`: there is no single app behind a class whose notifications arrive as ntfy channel messages over the cloud stream, and a header that opened an arbitrary one would be a lie about where these came from.
stack_msgs.title: RSS

stack_msgs._doc: The catch-all, and the reason this page cannot silently lose a notification. It draws every app the four classes above do not claim, so a newly installed messaging app is visible here from its first notification and stays visible until somebody decides which class it belongs to. It is last on purpose — it is a triage queue, not a destination.
stack_msgs.title: Other

tiles._doc: Camera — the fleet's OWN camera (ac_cloud-camera, applicationId cld.camera, our signed build of GrapheneOS Camera), not a third-party one. The owner asked for it 'as last' in this row on 2026-09-10, and LAST HERE IS ARRAY POSITION: GroupedTilesFragment walks group.tiles in declared order and applies no sort of any kind, so appending is what makes it last and reordering this array is the only way to move it. There is no `order` field to set and none is wanted — a second way to express position is a second thing to disagree with the first. target=extapp:cloud-camera → MainActivity.launchExternalApp opens cld.camera if installed, else downloads + installs ui.external_apps[id=cloud-camera].install_apk_url. icon ic_camera is its own drawable rather than ic_photos, which the Gallery tile already carries; Sections.iconResFor falls back to ic_link_tile without complaining when a name resolves to nothing, so a shared or misspelt icon is a silent defect and test-camera-tiles.sh pins the file's existence.

Same shape as Writer: target=extapp:cloud-calc → launchExternalApp opens the package if installed, else installs ui.external_apps[id=cloud-calc].install_apk_url (ABI-resolved through the fleet assets map). icon ic_calc is Cloud Calc's own launcher foreground, cropped to its art like ic_writer.

tiles._doc: Writer — hands off to the standalone Cloud Writer app (ac_cloud-writer, com.diegonmarcos.cloudwriter, read from ITS android.application_id and app/build.gradle namespace, not guessed from the slug). Same shape as the Keyboard tile beside it: target=extapp:cloud-writer → ShellActivity.launchExternalApp opens the package if installed, else downloads + installs ui.external_apps[id=cloud-writer].install_apk_url — no ACTION_VIEW, so there is no seventh ad-hoc startActivity site and no ActivityNotFoundException path. POSITION IS DELIBERATE AND IT IS NOT LAST: GroupedTilesFragment walks group.tiles in declared order with no sort, and the Camera tile below records the owner asking for the camera 'as last' in this row on 2026-09-10, so Writer goes in front of it rather than displacing a placement he named. icon ic_writer is Cloud Writer's own launcher foreground copied into this app's drawables — Sections.iconResFor falls back to ic_link_tile in silence when a name resolves to nothing, so the file's existence is pinned by test-writer-tile.sh rather than trusted.

tiles._doc: Drive, the leading tile of Data Apps. It used to be a `page:drive/connections` deep link into an in-app section; task 302/304 lifted those four tabs out into the standalone Cloud Drive APK (ac_cloud-drive, com.diegonmarcos.clouddrive), whose Files tab is a full native local file manager rather than a list of remote back ends. The tile now LAUNCHES that app through the `extapp:` resolver and ui.external_apps.cloud-drive. The tile id is unchanged because the Home tile rows address it by id. ICON — THIS TILE IS THE ONE PLACE THE DRIVE GLYPH IS DECLARED. The one-hand left-edge `down` sector carries no icon field of its own: libs/launcher-onehand/build.gradle derives action_catalogue from these tiles, canonicalising `extapp:cloud-drive` and `app:com.diegonmarcos.clouddrive` onto one key through ui.external_apps, and OneHandAccessibilityService.declaredIcon draws whatever this field names when the APK is not installed. Changing it here therefore changes the tile AND the edge sector, and there is deliberately no second field anywhere to disagree with it. It was ic_p_sol_cloud, a shared palette glyph four other entries also use and the mark the in-app Drive PAGE wore; task 404 made it ic_drive, which now holds Cloud Drive OWN launcher foreground copied verbatim from ac_cloud-drive/app/src/main/res/drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml — the same thing Writer, Camera and Nav already do for their extracted apps. Sections.iconResFor falls back to ic_link_tile in silence when a name resolves to nothing, so both the existence of that drawable and its provenance are pinned by test-onehand-app-sector-icon.sh rather than trusted.
tiles.label: Drive

tiles._doc: Divides Drive from the rest of Data Apps. Drive is about to stop being a page and become its own application (task 302/304), so it is no longer a sibling of Calendar and Contacts — it is the row's entry point. A CHARACTER and not a rule: `separator: true` makes GroupedTilesFragment draw a bare '|', not clickable, not focusable, hidden from accessibility, which is what the owner asked for — "add this char, not a line, a char!! a seprator". Same declaration as projects-me-sep-1, so Sections.TileGroup.destinations drops it and no surface that reads tiles as places to go ever offers it.

Cloud Notes (ac_cloud-notes, com.diegonmarcos.cloudnotes) — our own signed build of Cloud Notes, a local-first notes/whiteboard app. Formerly a Markor build in this same directory; #495 flipped the Cloud Notes build (vendored alongside it by #469 under com.diegonmarcos.cloud-notes) onto this identity and deleted the Markor tree. #522 put the DIRECTORY and the NAME back: the product is cloud-notes, Cloud Notes is only the upstream it is built from. Replaces the `obsidian://open` deep link this tile used to carry, back when it was added. Two things were wrong with that target and only one of them was about branding: it is a bare scheme URI, so ShellActivity.launchUri turns it into a plain ACTION_VIEW and it raises ActivityNotFoundException on any phone without Obsidian installed — the exact hazard test-drive-page-sections.sh T9 exists to contain, and a tile that fails AFTER the tap. `extapp:cloud-notes` resolves through ui.external_apps instead: installed → launches, absent → offers the install from the Constellation store. Obsidian itself is NOT removed from the phone or from this file — md.obsidian keeps its ui.phone_folders keyword and its place in the favourites picker (a favourite is what you can pick, not what you get), so nothing dangles.

tiles._doc: Cloud Tasks (ac_cloud-tasks, com.diegonmarcos.cloudagenda): tasks first, with the calendar, events and invites one tab away. Captioned by function, Tasks, since cloud-calendar became cloud-agenda (#315) and then cloud-tasks. The tile id stays `calendar` because the Home tile rows address tiles by id.

tiles._doc: Divides Notes and Tasks from the media pair, in the owner's order: Drive | Notes Tasks | Gallery Media News | Office. Same separator declaration as data-apps-sep-1.

Gallery — the Data Apps tile for cloud-gallery (ac_cloud-gallery, applicationId com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter), our Google-Photos/Samsung-Gallery replacement (local gallery + PhotoPrism cloud library + backup). Registered in ui.external_apps[cloud-gallery]; this tile is what makes it VISIBLE in the launcher — an external_apps entry alone only makes an app installable/openable BY ID and shows nothing. The app was called cloud-media-center until 2026-10 and this tile's id was mediacenter; both were renamed to gallery so that the name cloud-media-center could go to the new Tauri media app (ac_cloud-media-center, com.diegonmarcos.cloudmediacenter). The applicationId did NOT change, because the app is installed on phones and a new package id would be a different app to Android. The former sibling 'photos' tile (app://com.google.android.apps.photos) was removed 2026-08-30 — Gallery is the sole photo entry point.

tiles._doc: Media Center — the Data Apps tile for cloud-media-center (ac_cloud-media-center, com.diegonmarcos.cloudmediacenter), the Tauri media hub: music (TIDAL playlists), videos, gallery (Pinterest boards), books, the feed, movies and documentaries. It REPLACES the old Music tile, which launched TIDAL itself (app://com.aspiro.tidal); TIDAL is not removed from the phone — every track in the Media Center's music page opens a TIDAL search through the system, so the app is still one tap away. Resolved through ui.external_apps[cloud-media-center]: installed launches it, absent offers the install. Not to be confused with cloud-gallery (the Gallery tile above, com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter), which held the name cloud-media-center until 2026-10.

tiles._doc: Divides the media group from Office, in the owner's order: Drive | Notes Tasks | Gallery Media News | Office. Same separator declaration as data-apps-sep-1.

#380. This tile is the Data Apps entry for the application whose IDENTITY is cloud-office (ac_cloud-office, com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice) and its label is "Office" — a caption for the tap target, not a name for the app. It printed the identity string "cloud-office" until #380; identity now lives only in `target`/ui.external_apps[cloud-office].id and the app's own build.json::name, and nothing about the package, the Cloud-Office.apk asset or the folder changed with this label. THE PREVIOUS _doc HERE WAS WRONG TWICE AND IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN KEPT. It said "this tile label and ui.external_apps[cloud-office].label are the two names the fleet owns": ui.external_apps carries NO label key on any of its 23 entries, and test-app-names-pattern.sh T3 forbids one outright ("ui.external_apps shows the id and restates no name") — so that sentence pointed a future editor at a second copy that does not exist and would have reddened the guard the moment they created it. It also said the rebrand waits on build.json::build.host "and it is null"; ac_cloud-office/build.json::build.host is ubuntu-latest and the source build has published Cloud-Office.apk. Android's own home screen is a SEPARATE surface from this tile and takes its label from the APK manifest, via --with-app-name = that app's build.json::name, which test-app-name-reaches-the-user.sh pins to the cloud-<x> pattern — deliberately NOT to this caption.

tile_groups._doc: Me — the personal-administration row, in the owner's order: Me | Me-Health Experiences RoadMap | Me-Duties Me-Buro Me-LLC | Account ('|' = group separators, like the AGI row). Same `extapp:<appId>#<target>` hand-off as the tiles beside it: launchExternalApp opens Cloud-Me and passes everything after the '#' as the `shortcut_action` extra, which Cloud-Me's MainActivity resolves through the `page:<section>/<page>` grammar; not installed, the same download-and-install path every other extapp tile uses. The fragment names declared section/page ids of ac_cloud-me/build.json (test-dashboard-cross-app-deeplink.sh T3 proves they resolve).

sections._doc_active_apps: Phone-only "Active Apps" section at the top of SuitePhoneAppsFragment, directly above Last Apps. Lists apps that are STILL RUNNING — holding a foreground service open, or currently in the foreground — most recently active first (libs:datamanager AppUsageProvider.activeNow, replaying FOREGROUND_SERVICE_START/STOP and ACTIVITY_RESUMED/STOPPED so a START with no matching STOP counts as alive). It is deliberately NOT a recency ranking: recentUsed returned the same head of the list as Last Apps, so the two sections rendered as twins. An app you opened and then left behind, with no service and no visible activity, belongs to Last Apps and not here. Empty (section hidden) when usage-access is not granted. Baked to scalar BuildConfig fields UI_SUITE_ACTIVE_APPS_{ENABLED,TITLE,LIMIT}.
sections._doc_last_apps: Phone-only 'Last Apps' section rendered directly BELOW Active Apps, still inside the Quickmarks block at the top of SuitePhoneAppsFragment. Lists the `limit` apps you most recently OPENED, most recent first (libs:datamanager AppUsageProvider.lastOpened → UsageStatsManager MOVE_TO_FOREGROUND events over 7 days). Different data from Active Apps: that one ranks by `lastTimeUsed`, which the system also bumps for background work, so a sync adapter can outrank an app you actually launched; this one only counts an app being brought to the front. Empty (section hidden) when usage-access is not granted. Baked to scalar BuildConfig fields UI_SUITE_LAST_APPS_{ENABLED,TITLE,LIMIT}.

sections._doc_phone_app_groups:
Curated phone apps for Phone ▸ Apps ▸ Quickmarks. THIRD-PARTY ONLY: anything the constellation already offers a way into is reached from Cloud ▸ Apps, and SuitePhoneAppsFragment filters those out of this page's enumerated sections (All Apps, Smart Folders, Active Apps), so keep our own packages out of it here. On 2026-09-10 the two Cloud Terminal forks (cld.termux, cld.termux.nix) left the AI group, which is what that rule had been asking for since it was written — they were the only fleet packages in here. Group order = render order; each renders as a subhead + UI_PHONE_GRID_COLUMNS-col grid.

A MISSING PACKAGE IS NO LONGER HIDDEN, AND THAT IS THE POINT. This doc used to end 'Missing packages are silently hidden', and the sentence before it justified the third-party rule with 'a curated entry that never renders is worse than no entry'. Both described the same behaviour: resolve() returned null for an uninstalled package and mapNotNull dropped it, so a tile the owner had deliberately curated simply was not there and nothing said why. That is inverted as of 2026-09-10. A curated entry for a package that is not installed now renders as a PLACEHOLDER tile — outlined glyph, 'Not installed' caption, tap to install — so the list you wrote is the list you see. The old rule survives only where it was always right: the ENUMERATED sections (All Apps, Smart Folders, Active Apps) are built from what the device actually has, and a not-installed placeholder in a list enumerated from the device would be nonsense, so those still show installed apps only.

ENTRY SHAPE. An entry is either a bare package string or {"pkg", "label"}. `label` is the NOT-INSTALLED FALLBACK ONLY: an installed app always draws its own PackageManager label, so the two can never disagree on a real device. It exists because a placeholder has no launcher label to borrow and 'ch.protonmail.android' is not a name anybody recognises. Omit it and the tile falls back to the prettified last meaningful segment of the package id.
sections._doc_quickmark_never_installable: Packages that a curated entry must NOT name, because neither of the two outcomes a tile has is available for them. A curated entry resolves to a launchable app or to a placeholder offering to install it; these packages offer a third thing that does not exist — they are preinstalled so they never render the placeholder, and they expose no launch intent so the tile is a tap that does nothing. #249 asked what happens to an entry that can never be installed and this is the answer: it is not an entry. Each record below carries the honest alternative so the next reader does not re-derive it, and so that 'why is this missing' has a written answer instead of becoming a silent re-add. Asserted by test-phone-quickmark-placeholders.sh T10.

quickmark_never_installable.reason: Google Password Manager is a surface INSIDE Google Play services, not a standalone installable application. It has no package id and no launcher entry of its own. com.google.android.gms is the package that hosts it: preinstalled, so a placeholder tile never renders, and with no launch intent, so a plain tile is a dead tap. There is no package id that can carry this name.
quickmark_never_installable._doc_deep_link: The honest target, and a public stable URL rather than a Play-services-internal component name recalled from memory. On a device with Play services it opens Google Password Manager; worst case it opens the same manager in a browser. It is recorded and NOT wired up: a phone_app_groups entry is a package id by construction and T1/T2 enforce exactly that, so admitting an entry that declares a target instead of a package is a SCHEMA change to the quickmark shape, not a data edit. That change was not made unilaterally under this ticket — see the report for #249 for the sketch.

This list is the curated one, read by SuitePhoneAppsFragment out of BuildConfig.UI_SUITE_PHONE_GROUPS_B64, and it is the only one an owner can add a shortcut to. Nothing is shared between the two, so a package in one says nothing about the other and a test that only asks 'is the string in build.json' cannot tell them apart. THIS IS AN ADDITION, NOT A MOVE: the same package is also a keyword of ui.phone_folders[prod_utils] and stays there, because All-apps classifies everything installed and Quickmarks is a shortlist — an app on both pages is the normal case, exactly as _doc_acode_is_in_two_places already records for Acode. APPENDED because the owner named no position: SuitePhoneAppsFragment maps this array in declared order and chunks it into rows with no sort anywhere, so array position IS render position. It is last of eight rather than last of seven because miDNI landed in this same list first, from a different request; with UI_PHONE_GRID_COLUMNS = 6 that puts the camera in row two, second tile, and moving it is a one-line reorder here.

phone_app_groups._doc_surface: QUICKMARKS, and that is the whole point of this group. The owner asked for it 'after Tools Primary and Before Configs', and Configs exists on no other surface — ui.phone_sections (the All Apps taxonomy) has no such section — so the anchor named this array and only this array. It was first built on 2026-09-10 as a '#' section in ui.phone_sections instead, which is the page the owner was not talking about; that section is gone and the folders it held went back where they came from. Position is meaning here: this group sits at index 4, between Tools Primary and Configs, and SuitePhoneAppsFragment.parseGroups preserves array order with no sort anywhere, so the index in this file is the order on the screen.
phone_app_groups._doc_loose_tiles: Five LOOSE packages and exactly one folder, because a quickmarks group can hold both — see the AI, Inboxes and Data Apps groups above, which each carry `packages` and `folders` together. The All-apps renderer cannot do this (PhoneAppsFragment.renderAllApps draws a section as subhead + folder grid, with no slot for an app belonging to no folder), which is why building this on that surface forced a folder named 'Projects' inside a section named 'Projects'. Nothing here needs a folder but Money.
phone_app_groups._doc_google_health: com.google.android.apps.fitness is Google Fit, read as the owner's 'Google Health'. The other reading is Health Connect (com.google.android.apps.healthdata, known to this repo as libs/health HealthConnectGateway.PROVIDER_PACKAGE), which is a data broker with no interface to open rather than an app you work in. Swap the pkg if that was meant.
phone_app_groups._doc_clickup: ClickUp ships under its parent company, Mango Technologies — co.mangotechnologies.clickup. The guessable com.clickup.android resolves to nothing, and since 149c5b9 an unresolved curated entry renders as a permanent 'Not installed' tile rather than hiding, so a wrong id here is furniture on the owner's screen.
phone_app_groups._doc_folders: 'Folder."Money"(all bank apps)'. This file's own answer to which packages are the bank apps is the -Money folder in ui.phone_folders (svc_money, Services · Buro), so this list is that folder's twelve exact package ids — its thirteenth keyword is the `pkg^com.btg.pactual.` family rule, which is a classifier pattern and not something a tile can launch. Curating them HERE is a copy, not a move: quickmarks and All apps are two pages, and an app appearing on both is how every other group in this array already works. -Money stays in Buro untouched.

sections._doc_tile_groups: Themed sub-groups for the Suite. tile_groups is the canonical schema, read by three surfaces: (1) bottom-nav Suite SECTION page → GroupedTilesFragment renders one titled row per group; (2) Home Apps Suite card → flattens all groups into a single horizontal scroll strip (home_groups entry has no group_explode); (3) aggregatorTilesFor flat fallback if anything else asks. Single source of truth — edit here, all surfaces update.
sections._doc_label: Bottom-nav slot 5. What is left of the old Suite section once its Cloud half moved to sections[cloud]: the installed-Android-apps surface. Keeps phone_app_groups + active_apps, which app/build.gradle bakes into BuildConfig by looking the section up as id=='phone'. tabs stays true with a single page so adding a second one needs no code change.
sections._doc_tiles_configs: Phone ▸ Configs — the ANDROID system settings screens, as Intent-scheme URIs handed to Intent.parseUri. Data, not Kotlin: add a screen by adding a line. A device that lacks one answers 'No app handles' rather than crashing (launchUri wraps startActivity in runCatching).

sections._doc_tabs: C3 IS its two halves, so it wears the same tab strip every other tabbed section wears (SectionTabsFragment + libs:bottomnav PageTabsView, driven purely by `tabs` + the visible `pages` below). pages._doc: What the cloud IS — the container/stack dashboard that used to be the whole of Cloud ▸ C3, carried down one level unchanged. Reports are NOT here any more: they are output rather than structure, so the reports tile now lives in stack_observability. page:c3/reports itself is unchanged and still routes the same way. FIRST tab: structure before behaviour, and it is also the landing page, because SectionTabsFragment.startIndex falls to the first page with a blank `action`. The `|` divider is unaffected — it is positioned by indexOfFirst { action.isNotBlank() }, which is still Watchdog at index 2 whichever way the two content tabs are ordered.

Reports moved here from Topology: Topology is what the fleet IS, and a report is output, not structure. A facet renders this section's own stack_observability; `facet` needs no `is_aggregator` on the section, only a stack_<page id> to read.

pages.label: Watchdog
pages._doc: A LAUNCH tab, not a content tab: it carries no facet and no fragment, only the same `action` grammar Configs' Keyboard entry uses, so tapping it dispatches extapp:c3-watchdog and the C3 strip stays where it was. That reuses launchExternalApp verbatim — the app opens when com.diegonmarcos.watchdog is installed, and when it is NOT the user is told so and the APK from ui.external_apps[id=c3-watchdog].install_apk_url is offered, instead of a tab that does nothing. is_action is what stops it being counted as a page anywhere a page means content.

pages.label: Morpheus
pages._doc: The second LAUNCH tab, identical in shape to Watchdog above: dispatches extapp:c3-morpheus (com.diegonmarcos.morpheus), falling back to installing ui.external_apps[id=c3-morpheus].install_apk_url. Morpheus shipped recently, so the not-installed path is the COMMON one here, not the edge case.

pages.label: WatchTower
pages._doc: The third LAUNCH tab, identical in shape to Watchdog and Morpheus above: no facet, no fragment, only an `action`, so tapping it dispatches extapp:c3-watchtower (com.diegonmarcos.watchtower) and the C3 strip stays where it was. Not installed -> the user is told so and ui.external_apps[id=c3-watchtower].install_apk_url is offered. is_action is what stops it being counted as a page anywhere a page means content. THE APP IS BRAND NEW, so the not-installed path is the ONLY path until the first ship run publishes, exactly as Morpheus's _doc records of its own first days.
pages._doc_index: INDEX 4, AFTER MORPHEUS, and the position is the requirement rather than a detail of it - the owner asked for it 'beside Morpheus'. It is also what leaves the `|` divider alone: SectionTabsFragment positions the divider with indexOfFirst { action.isNotBlank() }, which is Watchdog at index 2 both before and after this insertion. Inserting anywhere BEFORE index 2 would move the divider and silently restructure the whole strip. test/test-watchtower-tab.sh asserts the index and the divider, not merely that the tab exists.
pages._doc_icon: ic_p_c3_reports - the page-family icon for output rather than structure, which is what an analytics read is. Deliberately NOT a new drawable: Sections.iconResFor falls back to ic_link_tile IN SILENCE when a name resolves to nothing, so an invented name would render as a generic link with no error anywhere.

stack_observability._doc: INDEX of this page, same contract as stack_topology's: every tile is an `anchor:` id resolved by StackAnchors against the cards below, so the row is a table of contents rather than a set of deep links. One tile per card (Analytics, GHA, Dagu, GH Repos, Gitea Repos, NTFY), in the same order the cards render below. A CARD ADDED BELOW WITHOUT A TILE HERE IS HALF A CHANGE: that is what task #78 ('add top Index card, fix broken+duplicated More row') fixed, so leaving the Analytics card out of this row would have been #78 regressing on the same page it was fixed on.
stack_observability.title: Index
stack_observability.subtitle: Jump to a card on this page

stack_observability._doc:
ANALYTICS — the glance. Every other card on this page is a FEED: the latest N things that happened. This one is the only card that counts rather than lists, and that is exactly what the owner asked WatchTower to be, stated at card depth: over the last `limit` runs per repo, how many ran, what share of the FINISHED ones went green, and how long ago the last green was.

WHY THE DENOMINATOR IS 'FINISHED' AND NOT 'ALL'. A run still in progress carries an empty `conclusion`. Counting those as not-green makes the rate sag every time the fleet is mid-build, which is precisely when somebody opens this page. Queued and running are neither green nor failed — they are not yet anything. renderRunStatsFeed divides by the finished count and says 'no verdicts yet' rather than '0%' when that count is zero, because a rate with an empty denominator is not a rate.

SOURCE, NOT A NEW KIND. kind=feed with a sixth `source`, per this page's own long-standing instruction: a new integration is a new `when` arm in AggregatorStackFragment.renderFeed plus a client, never a new panel `kind`. It reads the SAME GitHubFeed.runs() the GHA card above reads, through the same 15-minute cache, so the two cards cost ONE fetch per repo between them and cannot disagree about a number.

THE REPO SET IS THIS ARRAY AND NOTHING ELSE, the same contract the GH Repos card documents. Deliberately the same three as the GHA card below (android/cloud/front) rather than ac_c3-watchtower's five: this is the glance and stays narrow, the app is the detail and carries the wider set. Adding a repo here is a data edit, never a Kotlin one.

OPENING THE FULL THING: the card's summary row targets extapp:c3-watchtower, so a tap hands off to the app through the SAME single dispatch chokepoint every other row uses (onTileClicked -> routeTarget -> launchExternalApp) — no seventh ad-hoc ACTION_VIEW site (#156), and the click still fires exactly once (#195). It is NOT in the More row below: More opens 'the full page behind a card' and its tiles are ordinary page: targets into HIDDEN c3 pages. There is no page:c3/analytics, and inventing one to have somewhere to point would add an un-wired stub page to satisfy a row.
stack_observability.title: Analytics
stack_observability.subtitle: Delivery over the last 30 runs per repo · green rate, failures, last green

stack_observability._doc: Last 5 Dagu runs across EVERY registered DAG, most-recent-first — a real run HISTORY, not the old dagu_dags kind's one-row-per-DAG registry (that showed each DAG's latest run only; this can show the same DAG twice if it ran twice in the top 5). Backed by GET /api/v1/dag-runs?limit=5 (DaguRunsFeed.kt, aa_cloud-superapp-only per this task's scope — NOT a change to ab_cloud-libs-shared's DaguClient), confirmed live 2026-09-06 to already answer newest-first with `limit` honored server-side. c3-infra-api's own /workflows/dagu proxy is unrelated and unused here — this card, like the native page:c3/dagu list, talks to Dagu directly via DaguPrefs so there is one Dagu config on the device.
stack_observability.title: Dagu
stack_observability.subtitle: Last 5 Dagu workflow runs · status

stack_observability._doc: Last COMMIT per repo (limit=1, not the old 'latest 3') from the whole cloud + front family. THIS ARRAY IS THE REPO SET: AggregatorStackFragment.renderRepoCommitsFeed iterates Sections.StackPanel.repos and nothing else, so adding a repo is a data edit here, never a Kotlin edit. The list is every repo of the two families that GitHub actually answers 200 for, verified against api.github.com/repos/diegonmarcos/<name>. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, so nobody re-adds them: `cloud-android` and `cloud-unix` answer 301 and redirect to `cloud-u-android` and `cloud-infra-desktop` respectively — they are rename-aliases of repos already listed, and adding them would duplicate every commit; `cloud-mykonsole-dtk` answers 404, the upstream is gone and only the gitea mirror still remembers it; `front` (the ~30-project web monorepo) answers 404 too — it has no GitHub remote at all, and diegonmarcos.github.io is the published front site, which is why THAT is the front entry rather than `front`. Rate limit: this panel plus GHA share GitHub's 60-requests-per-hour anonymous quota, so GitHubFeed caches for 15 minutes, staggers the fan-out, and reports an exhausted quota as `rate limited` rather than as an empty repo. This SAME repo list (different `owner`) is reused verbatim by the Gitea Repos card below, so the two cards are directly comparable — same repos, two mirrors.
stack_observability.title: GH Repos
stack_observability.subtitle: Last commit per repo · cloud + front family

stack_observability._doc: Same 8 repos as GH Repos, one mirror over. `owner` is `diego` (infra-dat_gitea's org — see cloud-u-containers/infra-dat_gitea/src/build.json::gitea.org) rather than `diegonmarcos`: GiteaFeed.kt hits http://10.0.0.6:3002/api/v1/repos/diego/<repo>/commits directly (mesh-only, confirmed live and unauthenticated for these public mirrors — 10.0.0.x is already cleartext-allowed in network_security_config.xml), NOT the public git.diegonmarcos.com domain, which sits behind two-factor auth this app cannot complete. Gitea mirrors EVERY non-fork GitHub repo except cloud-vault (mirror_policy.exclude), a much longer list than these 8 — this card deliberately reuses the SAME curated family as GH Repos rather than all ~30+ mirrors, so the two cards read as 'the same repos, two remotes' instead of one card being a long unrelated scroll.

stack_observability.subtitle: Last commit per repo · gitea mirror

stack_observability._doc: Last 5 messages per channel, EVERY ntfy channel in one card — replacing the old three scope-split cards (Advisories/My channels/Cloud channels). No `scopes` declared: renderNtfyGroups already treats an empty scopes list as 'every channel', so simply not filtering is the whole change, not a new code path. `limit: 5` caps rows per channel group (paintNtfyGroup), separate from the Inboxes ▸ C3 Ntfy card below which reuses the exact same kind/stream unbounded. Channel list is resolved from ui.ntfy (this build.json's own mirror of cloud-u-containers/infra-obs_ntfy/src/build.json::topics[] — see _doc_ntfy) through NtfyScopes, so a channel added upstream appears here on the next build with no second list to edit.

stack_observability._doc: MORE — the full pages behind this tab's cards, plus (as of the five-feed-card rework) the two pages that lost their only referrer when Inboxes ▸ C3 Ntfy stopped being a signpost: `health` and `wg-mesh` below point at page:c3/health and page:wg/status, both HIDDEN pages that tile_row used to be the sole way into. Ordinary `page:` targets, no anchor grammar: this opens the PAGE, which carries what a card cannot (DaguFragment lists AND starts runs, the log viewer is per-VM, C3 health has its own scope-filtered view). Subordinate by position — it sits at the bottom, after the five feed cards — so the cards stay the first thing read. stack_topology._doc: INDEX of this page, not a set of deep links. Every tile is an `anchor:` target handled by StackAnchors inside AggregatorStackFragment: it scrolls this stack to the card that claimed the id, so the row is a table of contents for what is already below it rather than four ways to leave. The four `stack/*` ids address SUB-TABLES of the single `cloud_dashboard` Stack card — that card renders groups providers/dbs/mcpapi from data/cloud_services.json, and the group and subgroup headers it draws register their own anchors, so Providers · VMs · Dbs · APIs are addressable WITHOUT splitting one card into four panels the data does not have (VMs and Runners are both subgroups of `providers`; APIs and MCPs are both subgroups of `mcpapi`). WG mesh left this row: the WireGuard screen is Configs ▸ WireGuard (page:config/wg → WireGuardFragment) and does not need a second entry point here. Drive · Connections left it too and now lives under Cloud ▸ Apps ▸ Data Apps, pointing at the same page:drive/connections.

stack_topology.subtitle: Jump to a table on this page

stack_topology._doc: Heading over the two URL cards, so the Public/Private pair reads as one titled block the way 'Containers' and 'Stack' already do below. Same section_title kind — a plain heading between cards, not a card.
stack_topology.title: Addresses

stack_topology._doc: Routed URLs — what the fleet EXPOSES and where each name actually goes. Data-driven from data/services_public.json (43 rows), the same regen.sh snapshot the C3 Health page reads, so nothing is hand-listed here and nothing can rot out of step with the infra: the panel kind c3_public already renders exactly the wanted shape (name · auth · https://<public_url> · 🔒 <private_dns, which is host:port> · vm). TITLE SAYS 'routes', deliberately, NOT 'internet-reachable': services_public.json means A PROXY ROUTE EXISTS, and regen.sh never reads wg_only — eight sibling MCPs are wg_only:true yet appear here on mcp.diegonmarcos.com routes, mesh-gated with a 403 fallback. Claiming those are public would make this card assert something false about the security posture, which is worse than not having the card; per-row wg_only would be truer still, but it is not in the snapshot and inventing it here rather than in regen.sh is exactly the rot this file avoids.
stack_topology.title: Public URLs · proxy routes
stack_topology.subtitle: public host → upstream host:port · a route exists, not necessarily open to the internet

stack_topology._doc: The other half: containers with NO proxy route at all — reachable only over the WireGuard mesh. Data-driven from data/services_private.json (60 rows) via the existing c3_private panel kind (name · protocol/db · service · 🔒 <private_dns, host:port> · vm). Together with the card above this answers 'what is exposed and where does it actually go' from ONE generated source rather than from either Caddyfile — which matters because there are two of them (infra-sec_caddy on gcp-proxy = mesh side, infra-sec_caddy-public on oci-analytics = public edge) and because the public edge's repo dist is NOT what is deployed.
stack_topology.title: Private URLs · mesh only
stack_topology.subtitle: no proxy route — WireGuard host:port

stack_topology._doc: Cloud dashboard — section_title dividers + 3 collapsible cloud_dashboard CARDS. 'Containers' heading → Infra Apps + User Apps (every container exactly once). 'Stack' heading → the Stack card (free cross-cut lists: Providers/VMs · DBs · MCP & API). Grouping + inventory DATA-DRIVEN from data/cloud_services.json (BuildConfig.CLOUD_SERVICES_B64), generated by data/gen_cloud_services.js from cloud/a_solutions. renderCloudDashboard draws an icon grid (ui.tile_columns/line) with a STATUS LIGHT under each icon (TCP-ping over WireGuard) + opens the URL in the in-app browser on tap. `group`/`groups` selects which cloud_services.json group(s) a card renders.

stack_topology._doc_anchors: The sub-tables this ONE card provides as anchor targets, declared the way a section declares its pages: an `id` other tiles point at with `target: "anchor:<id>"`, plus the header inside this card it lands on. `group` alone binds to that group's header; adding `subgroup` binds to a sub-header under it. The id is NEVER derived from a label — renaming the "VMs" sub-header cannot rename `stack/vms`, it only breaks the binding, and test/test-stack-anchors-declared.sh fails on a binding whose group/subgroup is not in data/cloud_services.json. It also removes the old ambiguity where group "DBs (storage)" and subgroup "DBs" both slugged to `dbs`: `stack/dbs` says group, so it lands on the group header by declaration rather than by registration order.

stack_topology._doc: MORE — the same contract as Observability's row: ordinary `page:` targets to the full pages, sitting below everything the Index indexes so the table of contents is still read first. These two had no referrer anywhere in build.json once the Index became pure anchors. The distinction is real and not redundancy: `anchor:stack/vms` scrolls to the VMs sub-table inside the Stack card, while `page:c3/vms` opens the VMs PAGE, which carries per-VM detail the card's icon grid does not.

sections._doc: MyHealth — the PAGES are GONE: the Compose surface moved to Cloud-Me (Projects > Health), so there is one Health screen in the constellation instead of two copies of the same Health Connect reader, and the Cloud > Dashboard tile deep-links into it (extapp:cloud-me#page:health/home). This entry survives because libs:health/build.gradle looks the metric taxonomy up by SECTION ID — `ui.sections.find { it.id == 'health' }.metrics` — and Configs > Permissions still reads the result as HealthMetrics.allPermissions to count and request the 34 Health Connect grants. Deleting the section would silently turn that row into '0 / 0'. A pageless section is legal (Sections.kt: `optJSONArray("pages")` tolerates absent) and with no pages, no module and bottom_nav:false it is reachable from nothing.
sections._doc_metrics: Data-driven metric taxonomy — read by libs:health (UI_HEALTH_METRICS_B64) and by Configs > Permissions. Each metric maps to one-or-more Health Connect record types via `records` (matched at runtime by class simple-name) + the perm subset via `perm_keys`. This is now the SuperApp's only stake in Health: the pages that used to render these tiles live in Cloud-Me, which declares its own copy of this list for the same reason (its libs:health reads its own build.json).
sections.label: MyHealth
sections._doc_taxonomy: Metric grouping mirrors Health Connect's own UI categories (verified against es-ES locale: Actividad / Constantes vitales / Medidas corporales / Nutrición / Seguimiento del ciclo / Sueño) so the per-metric counts in MyHealth match exactly what the HC permission screen shows. Vo2Max sits under Activity (not Heart) per HC; Exercise stays under Activity (no separate Workouts category in HC). Total perms across all metrics = 34, matching HC's count when every category is granted.

sections.label: Configs
sections._doc_grid_columns: Icons per row of the Configs page grid: a fixed 8, declared here, NOT the Cloud/Phone stepper (GridColumns.cloud). 8 is GridColumns.MAX; at 360 dp a cell is 45 dp, the icon is 27 dp (cell minus 18 dp of margin, padding and the inline separator) and labels autosize 9 sp and end-ellipsize. A `separator` page takes no cell: it is a wrap_content character between tiles, as in Data Apps.
sections._doc_nav_mode: #1221 horizontal_two_rows: the second row of Configs is one row per declared group, each [group label] | [that group's page icons]. Fleet reads Bluetooth | C3 Fleet Control (| Peer Control); Observability reads Agents | Diagnostics Logcat About; Setup keeps the rest. Every page of the section is in exactly one group (the nav-shape guard, N10), the hidden tab pages with their parent. The groups only REFERENCE pages: the Configs grid headings still come from each page's group / subgroup.
sections._doc_pages_order: Order here is the single source of truth — it drives the Configs page-grid, its SECTION and SUBSECTION headings, and (via home_groups tiles_from_section: 'config') the Home Apps Configs row. TWO LEVELS, DECLARED PER PAGE (#649): `group` is the section heading a tile sits under and `subgroup` is the heading below it, both rendered verbatim by TileGridFragment — the words "Launcher", "Setup", "Apps", "Network" and "Observability" appear in no Kotlin file, which is the same contract `label` already keeps for a page name. There is deliberately no parallel group map: a run of consecutive pages carrying the same group/subgroup IS the group, so moving an entry in this array moves it on the screen and a group with no pages left simply stops being drawn. A page that declares no group falls under the default Pages heading, which is every other section in this file. #649 replaced the old flat shape (Account/WireGuard/KDE/AI/Permissions — Launcher — Store/About, held together by `row_break`): Launcher stopped being a page wearing four tabs and became the TITLE over its four subpages as direct tiles, and the rest became Setup ▸ Apps + Setup ▸ Observability. `row_break: true` still starts a fresh grid row at a tile without printing a heading; no page in this section needs it any more, because every row break here is now a group boundary. ACTIONS ARE UNCHANGED: the trailing `is_action` entries are the same three, rendered under the same Actions heading from the same flag, and they carry no group — the grid appends them last whatever their position in this array. #723 (#878 relabelled: group Watchdog is now Setup, subgroups Setup/Mesh are Apps/Network): OWNER REGROUP (Agents): the order is Launcher, Apps, Setup. Apps is a group with no subgroup and holds C3 · Peer Control · Agents (C3 and Peer Control moved out of Setup ▸ Network with their ids unchanged, so page:config/c3 and page:config/kde are the same links; the Network separator went with them, see removed_pages). Before that regroup, the Setup group had THREE sub-sections in this order — Apps (Account · Permissions · Store), Network (WireGuard · Peer Control) and Observability (About) — and the AI page is gone (see removed_pages). #REORG 2026-10: Configs is exactly THREE sections, in this order: Setup (subgroups Apps = Account/Permissions/Store, Launcher = Presets/Controls/One-Hand/Notify, Network), Fleet (the former Apps group: C3 · Peer Control · Agents) and Observability (About). No ids changed, so every page:config/<id> link is intact. #733: Network is Cloud Mesh (the wg page, relabelled) · Peer Control · Apps Mesh (the Store's mesh page, reached from here too).
sections._doc_retired_pages: #697. A config page id that no longer exists, mapped to the pages its content lives on now. The page set is guarded: test-configs-two-sections.sh T9 holds the ids as they stood before #649 regrouped this section and fails if any of them is missing from `pages` without being named here, or if a page named here is still declared, or if one of its successors is not. So a page cannot be dropped by a regroup — removing one is a declared act with a declared destination. `launcher` is the only entry: #649 dissolved the page that wore four tabs and made those four tabs direct pages under the Launcher heading. Read by the tester only; the app routes by `pages` and never needs to know what was retired.
sections._doc_removed_pages: #723. A config page id that was DELETED rather than moved, with the reason. Distinct from retired_pages on purpose: a retired page names the visible pages its content lives on now, and these have none in Configs — the owner removed the AI page outright because AI tokens are managed in Account (the vault cockpit AI card applies them), so the five-tab AI strip and every tab under it went with it, and the Account card's link to the page was removed rather than left pointing at nothing. Guarded by test-configs-two-sections.sh T9 (the id may not be declared, must have existed, must carry a reason) and T12 (no route, page: target or Kotlin branch may still name it). Read by the tester only.

It was Configs ▸ Home ▸ Notify, and Home's other tab, Push, was merged INTO it: the persistent-badge boxes now lead the page and Push's customization menus sit under the Filters as a collapsed Configs card. Then the page moved here and the emptied Home was deleted. `mirror_page` names sections[communication].pages[my-rss] and LauncherNavController.aggregatorPage renders that page's own fragment, so the cards, the filter row and the stack_my-rss declaration all stay owned by the Communication section — the two badge panes are stack_my-rss panels (kinds notification_badges / notification_badge_configs), not a copy declared here. mirror_page is the page-level twin of `mirror_section` (Cloud ▸ Configs / Cloud ▸ C3) and exists for the same reason those do: a tab that IS the other surface cannot drift from it, a second copy of it always does. Mirroring one PAGE rather than the section is what keeps this one tab instead of the Communication section's own six-tab strip nested inside ours. KEPT ITS ID: `hidden` keeps it out of the Configs grid while Section.allPages keeps `page:config/notify` resolvable, and the tab-owner lookup lands that target on this tab of Launcher.

pages._doc: ADB SHELL - THE page for the privileged channel (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools AdbShellPage), the same one Cloud Store (Settings), Cloud Account (Setup), the terminals (Settings) and every status chip draw. Six sections: the status table (Developer options, Wireless debugging, embedded adb, the local server on 38099, Shizuku, the active route and mode, each with a colour dot and when it was probed), Connect (the method that applies to the chosen mode, run step by step with the step that failed named), Active connection (Disconnect / Reconnect / Restart server / Stop server / Test round-trip, each disabled when it does not apply), Logs (an in-memory ring, tokens redacted, Copy and Clear), Declared needs (this app's privileged_channel above) and Setup (the checklist, each item opening its exact settings screen). pages._doc: #1263 Configs ▸ Setup ▸ Network ▸ WiFi: the phone's Wi-Fi analyzer as a page over libs:wifi (WifiFragment draws WifiPanel), right after ADB Shell. Five tabs over one process-wide controller, so scans, the throttle window and running tools survive a tab switch: Scan (live AP list: SSID / BSSID / vendor from the IEEE OUI asset, smoothed RSSI + sparkline, band / channel / width / centre, 802.11 standard, security incl. WPA3 / OWE / Enterprise / PMF / WPS, hidden, 802.11mc / az RTT, Wi-Fi 7 MLO, age; filter, sort, search, group by SSID; the scan throttle state), Channels (spectrum per band, channel rating and best-channel recommendation per regulatory plan, congestion, RSSI over time), Link (the connected network: speeds, frequency, signal / quality / SNR estimate, IPv4 / IPv6 / gateway / DNS / DHCP lease / MTU, captive / validated / metered / private DNS, MAC randomization, roaming log), Tools (ping / jitter / loss, traceroute, DNS, bounded port scan, LAN discovery via NSD / SSDP / sweep / NetBIOS, throughput to build.json wifi_analyzer.throughput, RTT ranging, hot / cold locator) and Log (heatmap grid, events, CSV / JSON / PCAP export and share). Vendors, channel plans and defaults are DATA in the lib's assets; this app's overrides are build.json wifi_analyzer. hidden tabs: reached through the WiFi strip.
pages.label: WiFi

pages._doc: #1221 Configs ▸ Fleet ▸ Bluetooth: the phone's Bluetooth as a page over libs:bluetooth (BluetoothFragment draws BluetoothPanel). ui._doc_launcher_themes: Launcher themes. `features` is the CHROME the theme draws; `toggles` is the DEVICE STATE it sets. Picking a theme applies both in one action, which is what the owner asked for: one tap, both effects. The mapping lives here and not in a Kotlin `when`, so a new theme is a new entry in this array and nothing else — no enum arm, no branch. Any toggle a theme does not name keeps its current value; a toggle marked `user_owned` in ui.launcher_settings.toggles is dropped from every mapping at parse time and can only ever be set by the user.
ui._doc_launcher_theme_surfaces: The Kotlin files that draw content under a launcher theme and must therefore take every colour from LauncherPalette. test-launcher-theme-palette.sh fails if any of them contains a colour literal again. THIS LIST ONLY GROWS: the rest of the app still paints literals chosen for the default gradient, and each file converted gets added here so the ground already won cannot be lost. Adding a file before converting it fails the tester, which is the intended order.

launcher_themes.label: Cloud Purple
launcher_themes.subtitle: The default rich SuperApp UI — bottom nav, dynamic island, 3D home. Top status strip trimmed to Time · Battery only.
launcher_themes._doc_palette: EVERY colour the launcher paints, named by ROLE and mapped to a res/values/colors.xml token (or, for `window`, a res/drawable). This is what a theme MEANS: before it existed a theme declared only behaviour flags, so picking one could reach the system bars, the chrome islands and the edge menu and could not reach a single pixel of content — the content painted 0xFF-literals chosen for the default gradient. A role missing from ANY theme fails test-launcher-theme-palette.sh, which is what stops the next theme shipping half-wired. Add a role here and it must be added to every theme; the hexes stay in colors.xml so the contrast checks and the Android resource qualifiers still see them.

launcher_themes.label: Cloud Minimalistic
launcher_themes.subtitle: Terminal aesthetic — pure black background, monospace green app list, no chrome. One-screen scroll.

ui._doc_launcher_profiles: Profiles the user can pick in Configs → Launcher → Profiles. The chosen profile is persisted via LauncherProfilePrefs. Unlike themes (which control UI/chrome/features), profiles control APP ISOLATION + DATA SAFETY — which apps the user can reach and which subsystems get neutered (e.g. Guest disables WireGuard so the guest can't see private infra). The `behavior` map is the declarative contract Push C reads. Personal = full access (passthrough). Work = same as Personal for now; tag-based filtering wires in once apps carry app_tags. Guest = hands-off lockdown.

launcher_profiles.label: Work
launcher_profiles.subtitle: Same as Personal for now — tag-based hide rules ship once each app/tile carries an app_tags list (e.g. work / personal / finance).

launcher_profiles.label: Personal
launcher_profiles.subtitle: Your default everyday profile — every installed app and folder visible.

launcher_profiles.label: Guest
launcher_profiles.subtitle: Locked down — only the system browser is reachable. WireGuard tunnel disabled so the guest can't see your private mesh. No SuperApp sections, no chat, no mail, no vault.

ui._doc_launcher_modes: Launcher MODES (Configs ▸ Launcher ▸ Presets ▸ Modes, #574): named bundles of the launcher's own switches — no chrome, no palette. `toggles` names ids from ui.launcher_settings.toggles and is applied by the SAME engine a theme's `toggles` go through (LauncherThemes.applyToggles), including the parse-time drop of `user_owned` ids; a switch a mode does not name keeps its value. The selected mode is persisted by LauncherModePrefs; 'modified' is DERIVED by comparing the device to this map, exactly as a theme's is. NOT the reverse of #435: that deleted power-saving theme was a theme with its own home pane, design vocabulary and system-lever engine — a mode here has none of those, only switches that already exist.

launcher_modes.label: Power Mode
launcher_modes.subtitle: Everything on — every animation, live stats, the 3D home, background polls. Full experience, full battery cost.

launcher_modes.label: Focus Mode
launcher_modes.subtitle: Quiet launcher — decorative animation, the dynamic island and message polling off, so nothing moves or interrupts.

ui._doc_launcher_presets: Configs ▸ Launcher ▸ Presets — the ONE declaration of what the tab shows: which groups, in what order, under what name, and which declaration feeds each. `kind` selects the renderer (profile → ui.launcher_profiles, theme → ui.launcher_themes, mode → ui.launcher_modes); the tiles' own names and order come from those arrays, so no caption is written in Kotlin and no id is ever displayed as a caption.

groups.label: Sandboxes

ui._doc_myfin_mock_tombstone: myfin_mock is GONE from the SuperApp, with the MyFin section and the libs:fin dependency that read it. The block now lives ONLY in ac_cloud-me/build.json::ui.myfin_mock, which is what libs:fin bakes into UI_MYFIN_MOCK_B64 for Cloud-Me's Buro > Fin.
