ui._doc_dynamic_island_action:
What happens when the user taps the dynamic-island pill in the toolbar. The supported forms are DECLARED in `_vocab_dynamic_island_action` — the SCHEMES, spelled without the colon so no other reader of this file mistakes the vocabulary for an `app:<packageName>` target of its own — and validated by app/build.gradle at configuration time: an absent key, a blank one, or a scheme that is not in that list FAILS THE BUILD. There is deliberately no fallback. `app:<packageName>` opens that app's launcher activity; `shortcut:<id>` fires one of the shell's shortcut intents. An uninstalled target falls back to a silent Toast, never to another surface, so the user's explicit binding stays the source of truth. #515 removed the `notifications` form: it opened the launcher's own drop-down shade, which was a second notification centre drawn from the same store as the Notify page, and that shade is deleted. The notification centre is the Notify page — ui.sections[communication].stack_my-rss, panel kind `notification_center`.

#675 ADDED THE `extapp` FORM AND RETARGETED THE PILL. The island is the SECOND of the two toolbar pills (the first is `music_playing_island`, the now-playing mini-pill, whose tap target is the package holding the live media session and is therefore not declarable here). It now opens cloud-myterminal through ui.external_apps[cloud-myterminal] rather than the UPSTREAM Nix-on-Droid package id it named before. `app:<packageName>` was the wrong form for a FLEET app: it resolves exactly one literal package, and when that package is absent it can only apologise. `extapp:<id>` is the constellation idiom the AGI Terminal tile and the Drive tile already use — ShellActivity.launchExternalApp walks fork → hub_package → altPackage and, when none is installed, offers the entry's install_apk_url (ABI-corrected from data/constellation-fleet.json), so an absent target becomes an install rather than a dead tap. The same replacement was made for the AGI Terminal tile in the #563 follow-up and for cloud-drive in task 302/304; the id `cloud-myterminal` is resolved by test-app-identity-resolves.sh T1, which fails if it has no ui.external_apps entry, so the binding cannot rot into a name nothing answers to. The upstream id is gone from this key on purpose: no fleet build installs com.termux.nix, so the previous binding could only ever reach a third-party app or a Toast.
ui._doc_app_tabs: App Tabs (libs:launcher-apptabs) — the last-N opened SuperApp entries (sections, pages incl. sub-pages, external apps) as an LRU grid. `cap` = how many to keep; MainActivity sets AppTabPrefs.cap from BuildConfig.UI_APP_TABS_CAP at startup.

app_tabs._doc: cap = how many entries the App Tabs LRU STORES (AppTabPrefs.cap, pushed in from BuildConfig at startup). star_cap = how many of them the Recent Tabs star DRAWS on its arc. Two numbers because they answer different questions: the store keeps a little more than any one surface shows, so an entry dropped by a filter (an external app, a page whose section was deleted) does not leave the arc short. star_cap must stay <= cap or the star can never fill.

ui._doc_search_scopes: Scope chips of the SuperApp's one search (search/SearchPanel.kt over libs:search's SearchEngine): the Home star (action:open_search, SearchSheetFragment), the Home swipe sheet and Cloud > Apps all show these chips. DECOUPLED from home_apps_tabs (renaming a search scope must NOT rename the Home-Apps body tabs). Each scope: `id` (also the result-section key), `label` (chip text), `section` (the title of its group of results), `kind` (which builder fills it). Results are one section per scope, in THIS order. Kinds: `cloud_apps` = cloud sections + tiles + every section's grouped rows (folder entries included) + home actions; `phone_apps` = installed launchable apps (LauncherApps); `cloud_configs` = every section sub-page + cached consolidated.json service entries (tap copies the value); `phone_configs` = installed Android Settings activities; `browser_fav` / `browser_history` = Cloud Browser's bookmarks / history matching the text, asked per query through its signature-guarded lookup provider (content://<cloud-browser>.lookup, never an incognito page), tap opens the page in Cloud Browser; `browser_web` = one row: Search the web for <text> with Cloud Browser's default engine, or Open <url> when the text is a URL or domain. No Cloud Browser (or one too old for the lookup): the browser scopes stay empty and say so once. Which chips start ON is per entry point (libs:search SearchEntry): Cloud > Apps and the swipe sheet start on the apps + configs, the Home star on the browser scopes + configs; each entry remembers its own last choice (search_scope_prefs). Reorder/rename here, no Kotlin edit.
ui._doc_camera_apps: Fallback camera apps for action:open_camera, in order. The FIRST attempt is always the OS resolver for MediaStore.INTENT_ACTION_STILL_IMAGE_CAMERA, which honours whatever camera the user set as default - this list is only for when nothing answers that action (some OEM cameras do not export the filter). Ordered so the OEM's own camera wins over a third-party one; a package that is not installed is skipped.
ui._doc_page_packages: Where each section's page implementations live: section id -> the packages under com.diegonmarcos.superapp that may hold its page classes (the Kotlin side of the page hierarchy). Read by PageImplementationsGuardTest, which fails when a declared page has no implementation (a page that has none must say `placeholder: true`), when launcher/SectionPages.kt routes a page no section declares (stale), or when a routed page class sits outside its section's packages. Sections whose pages are drawn from data (facet / tabs / url / upstream) or hosted by a lib module need no entry. Moving a page class means changing this map and the class's package together.
ui._doc_swipe_walk: Horizontal swipe (left/right) walk-list - the CIRCULAR ordered list of navigation stops the bottom-nav swipe-cycle steps through. Replaces the old 'cycle the 4 bottom-nav sections' behaviour: now it also visits each section's pages. Each stop: `section` (id in ui.sections) + an optional `page` (any page id of that section). Left-swipe = next (down the list), right-swipe = previous; wraps at both ends. Reorder/add/remove stops here - no Kotlin edit. Consumed by MainActivity.walkStep / Sections.swipeWalk(). Entries name a REAL section + page: infos-apps/infos-admin outlived the Apps|Admin facets Projects used to have and had been walking to page:infos/apps and page:infos/admin, neither of which exists — the walk step silently fell through to the section instead of the page.
ui._doc_phone_grid_columns: SHIPPED DEFAULT column count for the Phone tab's grids; 7 since the owner asked for it (was 6, which mirrored tile_columns). It is a default, not the value: Configs ▸ Launcher ▸ Controls has a stepper (4..8) that stores `grid_cols_phone` in the launcher_settings prefs, and GridColumns reads that first. A phone that never touched the stepper has no stored key and so follows this number, which is how the 6 -> 7 change reaches everyone who never chose a value while anyone who did choose keeps theirs. tile_columns is the same thing for the Cloud grids (`grid_cols_cloud`).
ui._doc_inbox_classes: CHANNEL CLASSES for Projects ▸ Inboxes (sections[infos].stack_msgs). A class answers one question — what KIND of channel did this arrive on — and a card on that page is one class. Declared here rather than inside the stack because a package roster is a CLASSIFICATION, and every classification in this file lives under ui.* keyed on package (phone_folders, ntfy.taxon, external_apps); a roster buried in a stack would be the only one no other surface and no tester could read. CLASSIFYING A NEWLY INSTALLED APP IS A DATA EDIT: add its package to a class's `packages`, or add its folder to a class's `folders`, and rebuild. There is no when(packageName) in Kotlin and there must never be one. A class draws its members from the UNION of two axes. `folders` names ui.phone_folders ids and takes every package that classifies into them, so a class that lines up with an existing folder writes down NOTHING and follows that folder for ever — mail is exactly this, which is why adding a mail client to phone_folders[prod_mail] puts it on the Mail card with no edit here. `packages` names exact package ids and exists for the classes the folder taxonomy cannot express: prod_chat holds Mattermost and WhatsApp and Telegram and ntfy together, so Chat and Messenger — which the owner asked to keep apart — cannot both be a folder. A package listed here must also be known to phone_folders, or this list would be describing an app the central taxonomy has never heard of. PRECEDENCE: an exact `packages` hit wins over a `folders` hit, so a single app can be lifted out of an otherwise-inherited folder without disturbing the folder. NO PACKAGE MAY APPEAR IN TWO CLASSES — a notification filed under two cards is drawn twice and counted twice, and test/test-inbox-classes.sh fails the build on it. THE CATCH-ALL IS NOT OPTIONAL. Exactly one class carries `catch_all: true`, and it receives every package the others do not claim. Four curated classes are not a catch-all and the per-app page they replaced was; without this the owner installs a messaging app, nothing classifies it, and its notifications quietly stop appearing on the screen they check. `source: c3ntfy` marks a class whose material is not phone packages at all but the ntfy CHANNEL stream — the same stream=channels renderer the C3 Ntfy panel uses. A class may declare both, and RSS does: the C3 channels over the cloud, plus the ntfy app's own notifications on the phone, which are the same messages arriving by the other road.

inbox_classes._doc: Every package ui.phone_folders already calls mail, and nothing written down twice. IMPORTANT — what this card can and cannot reach: mail NOTIFICATIONS, never mail CONTENT. The message bodies live in the mail app's own store, which this launcher does not read; ui.mail_accounts holds connection config and no messages. The card says so on itself.

Work and project-management-shaped rooms. Split out of prod_chat by hand because that folder cannot express it: it holds Mattermost next to WhatsApp. com.trello classifies into prod_plan (.Calendar & Tasks) for the launcher grid and is claimed here for this page — the two taxonomies answer different questions and are allowed to disagree, which is why `packages` beats `folders` rather than merging with it.

Strictly personal messaging, as the owner listed it: WhatsApp, WhatsApp Business, Instagram Direct, Messenger, Telegram 'etc...'. im.vector.app (Element) is here and not in chat because the card this page used to carry called it Messenger already. com.instagram.android is the Instagram app; its Direct DMs arrive under that package and there is no separate Direct package to name. The two SMS packages are here because a text message is a personal message however the carrier delivered it. THE DIALER LIVES HERE, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A DEFAULT. ui.inbox_classes replaced the four kinds of task #175 — mail, chat, messenger, DIALER — with the four the owner named on 2026-09-10 — Mail, Chat, Messenger, RSS — so the dialer stopped being a class of its own and had to land somewhere. Left unnamed it fell to the catch-all and sat in Other beside every app nobody had classified, which is the same visibility a missed call had before #175 gave it a box, so the regroup would have quietly undone #175 while passing every test. It is filed as Messenger because a missed call from a person is a one-to-one personal message and the class is already the home of every other one-to-one channel, SMS included. com.diegonmarcos.comms.dialer is the Cloud Dialer fork (ui.external_apps[cloud-dialer], Fossify Phone); it classifies into prod_phone for the launcher grid and to Messenger here, the documented explicit-beats-folder override, because the grid answers 'where is the app' and this page answers 'what kind of channel did this arrive on'. TO MOVE IT: delete the package from this list and it returns to Other, or name another class — one line, plus the line in test/test-inbox-classes.sh T8 that records the destination, which is deliberate: this decision may be changed but it may not be changed silently.

C3 ntfy channels and nothing else, which is what the owner asked for — `source: c3ntfy` reuses the stream=channels renderer verbatim, so this class is a title and a summary rather than new plumbing. io.heckel.ntfy is listed too: it is the ntfy client on the phone, so its notifications ARE C3 ntfy messages taking the other road, and filing them anywhere else would split one channel across two cards.

THE CATCH-ALL. Declares no members and needs none: it is every package the four classes above did not claim. Deleting this entry, or dropping its catch_all flag, makes this page capable of silently losing a notification, which is the one failure it exists to prevent. test/test-inbox-classes.sh asserts an unclassified package lands here.

ui._doc_phone_folders: Every launchable app is routed to exactly one folder by PhoneAppClassifier: folders are walked in `order`, and the first keyword that matches wins, so a lower order beats a higher one. Keyword forms: (1) `pkg:com.foo.bar` exact packageName; (2) `pkg^com.foo.` packageName.startsWith; (3) `lbl:name` exact case-insensitive label; (4) `lbl~frag` label contains (min 3 chars); (5) a bare string matches anywhere in "packageName label" (min 4 chars) — sweeping and collision-prone, so it is used sparingly. Every app installed at the 2026-09-07 rebuild is pinned with an exact `pkg:` rule, which is why the folder lists read as inventories; `pkg^` rules only cover families that will keep growing (our own com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.*, com.termux.*, VPN vendors). An app no keyword claimed then goes through the METADATA pass before any sink: `match_metadata`, declared beside `match_keywords`, routes on what Android itself publishes about the package, so a newly installed app is placed without a keyword edit. Three rule forms: `cat:game` matches ApplicationInfo.category by the platform constant name lowercased (game, audio, video, image, social, news, maps, productivity, accessibility); `intent:android.intent.category.APP_EMAIL` matches a launcher intent category the package resolves for, i.e. a role the platform grants it; `perm:android.permission.BODY_SENSORS` matches a permission declared in its manifest. Precedence inside the pass is by SIGNAL STRENGTH, not by `order` — category (the app states its own genre) beats intent (the platform grants it a role) beats permission (we infer from what it asks for), and `order` only breaks ties within one signal; otherwise a storage permission on a game would beat cat:game purely because Storage sorts earlier. Keywords always win over metadata: the keyword lists are curated and correct, metadata only keeps an un-curated app off the sink pile. Two sinks, neither with any rules: `others` (order 930, sink=true) catches everything both passes missed and is the triage queue — an app landing there means it needs a rule; `misc` (order 910) is the manual exile, give it explicit keywords to push something there on purpose. Neither carries a section prefix, so both render last under the Other subhead. The `match_keywords` lists cover THIRD-PARTY packages only: a keyword for one of our own constellation apps is derived at load time from ui.external_apps[].folder and must not be written here as well, or the identity would have two copies again and they could disagree. Manufacturer (Google / Samsung / non-Play-Store) is metadata for Smart Folders (see phone_smart_folders below) — NOT a primary grouping criterion. Order is a three-digit string, one hundred-block per section in phone_sections order, folders alphabetical by label inside the block (110, 120, ...); it drives both render order and match precedence, so a new folder takes the next free number in its block.

phone_folders._doc_label: Renamed from '_Dev & Terminal' to '_Dev' on 2026-09-10, when every terminal left for prod_terminals below. THE LEADING UNDERSCORE IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT PART OF THE NAME THE OWNER READS: ui._doc_phone_sections buckets a folder into a section by its label's FIRST CHARACTER, and '_' is Tools · System. Renaming this to a bare 'Dev' would not rename the folder, it would evict it — a label matching no declared prefix belongs to no section and renders last, down with the Misc and Others sinks. test-phone-taxonomy-prefixes.sh asserts this across every folder so the next rename cannot make the mistake quietly.

phone_folders._doc_whats_left: After the 2026-09-10 surgery this folder keeps MacroDroid, Google Admin, Google Analytics, Parallel Space, AutoClicker and Shizuku, plus our own com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.*/ide.* families and the three constellation apps that name it from ui.external_apps (cloud-myterminal, c3-watchdog, c3-morpheus). It is thinner but it is not empty, so it was NOT deleted — that is the owner's call to make, not this commit's.

phone_folders.label: @Mail
phone_folders._doc_match_keywords: This list is the CENTRAL classification: it is what puts a mail app in the "@" section, and therefore what makes its notifications survive the Notify ▸ Inboxes filter (PhoneTaxonomy.sectionPrefixOf → the first character of this folder's label). Any THIRD-PARTY package named as a mail client anywhere else in this file has to appear HERE too, or that other list is describing an app the taxonomy has never heard of (our own mail app is not in this list any more — it names this folder from ui.external_apps[cloud-mail].folder instead): app.sterna was added to sections[phone].phone_app_groups[Inboxes] on 2026-09-09 and not here, so upstream Sterna Mail fell to the `others` sink, came back prefix-less, and was pruned from every Notify tab except All. Keyed on package, never on label — the 2026-09-09 mail rename changed the product name and left every package id alone, which is exactly why this key survived it.

phone_folders._doc:
Every terminal on the device, gathered out of sys_dev on 2026-09-10 at the owner's request ('move all Terminals inside a folder called Terminals in the section Tools Inboxes & AI'). WHAT COUNTS AS A TERMINAL was read off what sys_dev actually held rather than off the names: the seven exact ids below plus the two startsWith families are precisely the termux-lineage entries that were in it, in both the upstream (com.termux*) and the fleet-fork (cld.termux*) namespace. Acode joins them because the owner put it here explicitly — it is an editor, not a shell, and it is here because he said so.

THE TWO pkg^ RULES HAD TO COME TOO. 'pkg^com.termux.' and 'pkg^cld.termux.' are the startsWith families that catch a termux sibling nobody has declared yet (termux-api, termux-boot, a future addon). Leaving either behind in sys_dev — order 310, which is walked before this folder's 460 — would have kept every such app in _Dev while the seven named ones moved, and the folder would have looked correct in the diff and been wrong on the device. Note that pkg^com.termux. does NOT cover the bare 'com.termux', and pkg^cld.termux. does not cover 'cld.termux', so both exact ids are listed as well.

The cld.termux* ids are OUR forks and ui._doc_phone_folders says fleet packages belong in ui.external_apps[].folder rather than in a match_keywords list. #571 gave cld.termux that entry (ui.external_apps[cloud-terminal-termux], folder prod_terminals), so its exact pkg: keyword left this list and is derived from the entry instead. The #563 follow-up did the same for cld.termux.nix once ui.external_apps[cloud-terminal-nix] existed: its exact pkg: keyword left too, derived from that entry's folder prod_terminals. cld.termux.nix.boot has no external_apps entry (it is a lib, not an app the AGI row launches) and stays here verbatim.
phone_folders.label: @Terminals

phone_folders._doc_match_keywords: Keyed on package because that is the only thing that survives a rename. pkg:com.collabora.libreoffice WAS in this list and is now GONE. It was here for the reason prod_mail states for its own list — a third-party package named anywhere else in this file has to be classified HERE too, or it lands in the `others` sink, comes back prefix-less and is pruned from every Notify tab except All while the launcher grid files it under Docs & Notes from ui.external_apps.folder, the two surfaces disagreeing about the same app — and it could not arrive by metadata instead, because PhoneAppClassifier matches `cat:productivity` against ApplicationInfo.category and refuses CATEGORY_UNDEFINED while upstream's manifest declares no android:appCategory at all. NONE OF THAT HOLDS ANY MORE. As of 2026-09-16 this fleet builds and publishes its own Cloud-Office.apk and ui.external_apps[cloud-office] names com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice, so com.collabora.libreoffice is no longer named anywhere in this file and nothing has to classify it. NO KEYWORD REPLACES IT AND NONE MAY BE ADDED: PhoneFolders derives the keyword for com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice from that entry's `folder`, so a literal here would be a second copy of an ownership the entry already holds — which is what test-app-identity-resolves.sh T8b reported twice while this line stood.

=Utilities
phone_folders._doc_samsung_camera: The Samsung stock camera (com.sec.android.app.camera) is HERE because the owner asked for it in Tools · Primary on 2026-09-10, and this is the general-purpose folder of that section — the same landing the last such request got, one entry below. IT IS A MOVE, NOT A COPY: it lived in .Storage (prod_storage, order 530) with the gallery and the two other camera apps until this commit, and prod_storage is walked BEFORE this folder, so leaving the old keyword behind would have kept it in .Storage while the diff read as done. Moving it back is one line — delete this keyword and restore pkg:com.sec.android.app.camera to prod_storage.match_keywords. NOTE WHAT DID NOT MOVE: pl.mobimax.cameraopus (Camera Opus, third-party) and cld.camera (our own Cloud Camera, whose classification now comes from ui.external_apps[id=cloud-camera].folder rather than from a keyword) both stay in .Storage. prod_storage still carries the metadata rules cat:image and intent:…APP_GALLERY, but the keyword pass runs across every folder BEFORE the metadata pass (PhoneAppClassifier.classify), so the keyword below is what decides and no gallery rule can pull the camera back.
phone_folders._doc_midni: miDNI (es.gob.interior.policia.midni) is the Spanish National Police's digital DNI, and by the Service/Tool split at the top of this file it is a SERVICE — it is worthless without the provider, and ui._doc_phone_sections names 'government and identity' as Buro's own territory; it lived in -Gov & ID until 2026-09-10. The owner asked for it in Tools · Primary and that is where it is. Recorded here rather than argued: identity you must produce on demand is something you reach for like a calculator, not something you file like a tax return, and where an app SITS is the owner's call. Moving it back is one line — delete this keyword and restore it to svc_gov.

phone_folders.label: *Nutrition
phone_folders._doc_match_keywords: The owner asked for a Nutrition folder under Tools · Health on 2026-09-10. FatSecret is the ONLY nutrition application this file declares — the whole keyword inventory was searched for the obvious siblings (MyFitnessPal, Yazio, Lifesum, Cronometer, a water tracker) and none of them is in it, and no device was reachable to enumerate what is actually installed. So this folder ships with one member rather than with a guess: an invented package id would render as a permanent 'Not installed' tile, and a folder with no rules at all is rejected by test-phone-taxonomy-prefixes T1. Name the others and they belong here. Google Fit stayed in *Outdoor & Sport: it counts steps, it does not count food.

ui._doc_phone_sections: Top-level section headers in the Home Apps/Phone tab. Folders are bucketed under a section by their label's first character: Services · Buro (-), Services · Others (+), Tools · System (_), Tools · Inboxes & AI (@), Tools · Data Apps (.), Tools · Primary (=), Tools · Media (>), Tools · Health (*). A folder whose label starts with none of those prefixes belongs to no section and renders last (that is where the Others and Misc sinks live). The split is Service vs Tool: a SERVICE is a client for one external provider you hold an account, contract or booking with, and is worthless without that provider (Santander, Ryanair, Uber, Airalo, ImmoScout24, Gov.br); a TOOL is software that operates on your own data or device and works with any provider or none (maps, file managers, notes, keyboards, browsers, media players). Entertainment clients are tools, not services: you reach for Netflix the way you reach for a media player. Tools · Inboxes & AI is everything that carries messages in and the assistants you talk to: AI, Chat, Mail, Phone & Contacts, News & Reading — it sits ahead of the other tool sections because it is what you open first and most. Tools · Data Apps holds the tools that own a body of your data (Calendar & Tasks, Docs & Notes, Storage); Tools · Primary holds the general-purpose ones that operate on whatever you point them at (Maps & Weather, Utilities, Web). Tools · Media is what you watch, listen to and play; Tools · Health is what you open to look after yourself — moving your body, learning something, staying informed. Services then split again by why you open them: BURO is the paperwork of being alive, the accounts you must keep in order (money, government and identity, telecom, housing, health, getting to work); OTHERS is discretionary, the services you open because you chose to (travel, shopping, events, jobs). Order = render order. Empty sections (every folder empty) are silently skipped. Phone tab renders one subhead per non-empty section + the folder grid below. PROJECTS IS NOT A SECTION HERE AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE. It was added as a '#' section on 2026-09-10 and removed the same day: the owner asked for it "after Tools Primary and Before Configs", and Configs exists only in sections[id=phone].phone_app_groups — the QUICKMARKS page — so the anchor named that array, never this one. It lives there now, at index 4. The difference is not cosmetic: a quickmarks group carries `packages` and `folders` together, so it can hold five loose applications beside one Money folder, while a section here is rendered as subhead + folder grid and has no slot for an app that belongs to no folder — which is what forced a folder called Projects inside a section called Projects, and what the owner objected to by name.
ui._doc_phone_smart_folders: Smart Folders rendered at the BOTTOM of the Home Apps/Phone tab — dynamic filters over the same LauncherApps.getActivityList enumeration the page uses. Apps still belong to their topical folder above; Smart Folders are an orthogonal cross-cut view by manufacturer / install-source. Rule types: pkg_prefix (any pkg starts-with one of values); pkg_eq (any pkg equals one of values); fleet_kind (any pkg that is a constellation-fleet member whose kind — 'app' or 'lib', taken from the CENTRAL classification data/regen.sh → constellation-fleet.json → BuildConfig.CONSTELLATION_FLEET_B64 — is one of values; splits OUR OWN APKs from the companion libraries off the registry, never a hand-maintained package list); install_source_in (the app's install-source-of-record — installingPackageName OR initiatingPackageName from PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo — IS one of values; use this to bucket apps by the store/installer that owns their updates); install_source_not (install source NOT in values — legacy catch-all for 'anything outside the official stores'); recently_installed (ranking rule: newest firstInstallTime first, capped at `limit`); recent_used (ranking: most-recently-used first via UsageStatsManager.lastTimeUsed, capped at `limit`); active_since (ranking: apps used within the last `window_h` hours, most-recent first, optional `limit`); most_opened (ranking: launch count via MOVE_TO_FOREGROUND events over 7d, capped at `limit`); top_network (ranking: total bytes rx+tx via NetworkStatsManager over 7d, capped at `limit`); top_battery (ranking: estimated mAh via libs:battery EnergyWatchdog.perAppEstimate, capped at `limit`). The five usage/network/battery ranking rules read through libs:datamanager (usage+network) / libs:battery (energy) and ALL need the PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS usage-access grant — without it each degrades to an empty (hidden) folder. The install-source values are real installer package names — verified on-device via /api/phone/classify (which dumps installing/initiating/system per app): com.android.vending=Google Play, com.sec.android.app.samsungapps=Galaxy Store, com.uptodown=Uptodown, org.fdroid.fdroid=F-Droid, com.google.android.packageinstaller=manual sideload (raw APK, no store), com.epicgames.portal=Epic, com.facebook.system=Meta's own installer.

phone_smart_folders.title: Cloud Apps
phone_smart_folders._doc: The constellation fleet's REAL apps (superapp, browser, vault, wallet, nav, ide, office, gallery, drive, comms.*, cld.* …) — each declared kind=app in its own build.json::release.kind. Driven from the CENTRAL classification (data/regen.sh → constellation-fleet.json → BuildConfig.CONSTELLATION_FLEET_B64) by the fleet_kind rule, NOT a hand-maintained package list: a new app that declares kind=app lands here and in nothing else, and a library reclassified lib leaves automatically. THIS FOLDER'S ENTIRE CONTENT IS THE FLEET'S OWN APKS, so on the merged Suite→Phone page it declares include_constellation: true — it is the EXCEPTION to that page's master exclusion that drops constellation packages, and the flag lets it see the full list while every other smart folder still filters them out. Declared here next to the folder, never hardcoded by id in Kotlin.

phone_smart_folders.title: Cloud Libs
phone_smart_folders._doc: The constellation fleet's companion APKs that are really libraries — lib-* modules (com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.*) shipping AIDL-bound engines, keyboard-engines (com.diegonmarcos.cloudkeyboardlibs), termux-boot (cld.termux.nix.boot) — each declared kind=lib in its own build.json::release.kind. Same central classification as Cloud Apps: the fleet_kind rule keeps only installed packages whose kind is lib, so a new lib module registers itself and no hand-maintained list here can drift. Same include_constellation: true exception as Cloud Apps, for the same reason — this folder IS the fleet's libs, so the merged page's master exclusion would strip away everything it exists to show.

phone_smart_folders.title: Google Play
phone_smart_folders._doc: Apps whose install-source-of-record is the Play Store itself, regardless of package name.

phone_smart_folders.title: F-Droid · Sideload
phone_smart_folders._doc: F-Droid installs PLUS raw-APK sideloads (com.google.android.packageinstaller = installed by hand, owned by no store). These get no automatic Play/Samsung updates.

phone_smart_folders.title: Direct
phone_smart_folders._doc: Sideloaded APKs not owned by any known store (raw install, e.g. via file manager/ADB). Anything whose install source is NOT one of the recognized stores below.

phone_smart_folders.title: New Apps
phone_smart_folders._doc: The 7 newest installs by firstInstallTime, capped at `limit`. `recently_installed` is a ranking rule (sort + take), not a per-app filter — PhoneSmartFolders.select handles it; no `values` needed.

phone_smart_folders.title: Recent 7
phone_smart_folders._doc: The 7 most-recently-used apps (UsageStatsManager.lastTimeUsed, 30d lookback). Ranking rule via libs:datamanager AppUsageProvider.recentUsed. Needs usage-access — empty (hidden) without it.

phone_smart_folders.title: Recent 48h
phone_smart_folders._doc: Apps used within the last 48 hours, most-recent first. Ranking rule via AppUsageProvider.activeSince(window_h). `limit` optional (0 = show all in-window). Needs usage-access.

phone_smart_folders.title: Active Apps
phone_smart_folders._doc: Apps used within the last 2 hours — the shortest active_since window, distinct from Recent 48h.

phone_smart_folders.title: Top 7 Open
phone_smart_folders._doc: The 7 most-opened apps by launch count (MOVE_TO_FOREGROUND events, 7d) via AppUsageProvider.mostOpened. Needs usage-access.

phone_smart_folders.title: Top 7 Battery
phone_smart_folders._doc: The 7 heaviest apps by estimated energy (mAh) via libs:battery EnergyWatchdog.perAppEstimate (AccuBattery-style: foreground-time × avg discharge mA). Needs usage-access.

phone_smart_folders.title: Top 7 Time Usage
phone_smart_folders._doc: The 7 apps with the most total foreground time (UsageStats.totalTimeInForeground, 7d) via AppUsageProvider.mostUsedTime. Needs usage-access.

ui._doc_profile_sync: Where the user profile is mirrored so the fleet operator has an out-of-band contact channel when the update chain breaks. ui._doc_profile: #778. The Configs → Account tab strip, in RENDER ORDER — exactly FOUR tabs, each {id, label}; the LABEL is the only user-visible word and lives only here. connect (sign in on the declared lines — ui.profile.connect — and fetch the declared server file, cloud-vault Shared/configs/profile-secrets.json, into app storage as S), profiles (the declared config held in app storage — the local copy L, else S — per topic: the vault sections of ui.profile.infos.schema, every field filled or empty, secrets masked; Populate from runtime, Populate from the server file, Save, Export), runtime (what each fleet app is using right now, read live per app — the apps and the vault sections each consumes are ui.vault_connect.cockpit.sections, how each is reached is its `runtime` block — with status reachable / not installed / not reporting) and drift (S, R and L side by side with metadata, the pairs of ui.profile.drift.pairs diffed per app and per field, and the sync actions). Restructured from #695's Connect | Infos | Cloud Constellation Setup: Infos became Profiles, Setup became Runtime (its index, wizard, cockpit cards and repos deleted; per-app apply moved to Drift's server → runtime). ProfileFragment maps id → column and nothing else about the strip is spelled out in Kotlin; test-account-four-tabs.sh pins this array (a fifth tab, a dropped or reordered tab, or a label moved into Kotlin goes red).

profile._doc_connect: #695 THE SIGN-IN LINES of Configs ▸ Account ▸ Connect, rendered as step 1 of the #573 journey. Each line is one place to sign in and each of its ways is one pill, side by side: `kind` is the ONLY thing ProfileFragment dispatches on. authelia_web / authelia_bearer are libs:auth's own sign-in kinds (auth.sign_in in ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json): the pill hosts the SHARED SignInWays narrowed to that one provider, so the dialog, the session cookie and the bearer store are the ones cloud-drive uses — never a copy. github_ssh_pat is this page's read of the vault export out of the private vault repo (auth.config_source.git.repo @ ref, path `vault_file`): an SSH key (JGit clone, bare, depth 1, deleted after) or a pasted token (the contents API, `github_contents_url`, raw), used once and never stored. A way whose kind this app does not dispatch renders its `note` as the reason it cannot start — never a dead button. gh_auth_login is GitHub CLI's own sign-in, carrying GitHub's public client inside the gh binary; the fleet registers NO GitHub OAuth app or credential pair of its own. #713: this APK still ships no gh — it BINDS the gh engine (Cloud-Lib-Gh.apk, top-level `engines.gh`, profile/GhEngine.kt), the way names its git_chain rung (`rung`, whose `host` gh signs in to), the code page opens in cloud-browser (auth.browser_mission's package), and the token gh then holds reads `vault_file` once through the PAT's read, never stored. Every way of every line is the same pill (FleetCockpitView.pill); nothing renders on Connect below the vault export. `note` on a line is what that line cannot do yet, stated plainly. #711 THE THIRD LINE, Import File, is the no-sign-in alternative: kind vault_file opens the system file picker and hands the picked bytes to the SAME classifier the Configs ▸ Import page uses (libs:auth VaultFile.classify, via ImportConfigsFragment.classify) and, when they are the DECRYPTED vault export (the #566 emitter's profile-secrets.json), to the SAME landing every sign-in uses (landVault) — so Infos fills and Cloud Constellation Setup unlocks exactly as after a fetch. Anything else (sops-encrypted, not JSON, empty, unknown schema, the paste-shape blob, unrecognised sections) is refused in red with the Import page's own sentence for it; nothing is stored. Order of the three lines is render order; test-account-four-tabs.sh pins it.

lines.label: Authelia → Gitea
lines.note: Cloud git (gitea) rides this same Authelia session in cloud-drive, but through the public edge gitea does not yet know who you are: private repositories stay invisible there until the fleet identity is mapped to a gitea user. Signing in here also fetches the vault configs, through the fleet's vault route and the one-time code it mails to your address.

ways.label: WebAuth
ways.note: GitHub CLI's own sign-in (gh auth login, GitHub's public client inside gh), run by the gh engine (Cloud-Lib-Gh.apk, engines.gh). The page to enter the code opens in cloud-browser. The token gh then holds reads the vault export once, exactly as a pasted PAT does, and is never stored by this app.

profile._doc_drift: #778 Account ▸ DRIFT, as data. Three files in ONE pattern (the vault bundle's `section › key › …` shape, AccountStore: {_meta {file, source, sha256, at}, body, apps}), stored side by side in app storage (an EncryptedFile per slot under filesDir/account): S = the declared server file as Connect last fetched it, R = the runtime snapshot (every value an app reported, at the vault path it is declared under), L = the local declared copy edited on this phone and not yet uploaded. `pairs` are the comparisons the tab offers, in order (a comparison with R is limited to what R observed: an app that cannot read a field is never drift). `upload` is where Upload L → server commits, through GitHub's contents API with the credential Connect holds (gh's token, else a PAT asked for once and never stored), on auth.config_source.git.repo @ ref: NOT profile-secrets.json itself — that file is GENERATED by cloud-vault's emit.py and guarded against hand edits on every push (vault-security-guard), so a phone commit there would turn the vault red and be overwritten by the next emit — but the declared local copy beside it, which emit.py validates (check-local) and diffs against the server file (local-diff) so the owner folds it into the sources. `message` placeholders: {device}, {fields}. `runtime_deadline_ms` bounds the wait for a serving app's binder (binding is what wakes a stopped app).

upload.message: profile-local: the declared copy from {device} ({fields} fields differ from the server file)

profile._doc_infos: #695 THE INFOS READ-OUT is the FETCHED vault configs and nothing else: one card per section of the bundle a Connect way fetched (order and labels from the vault's own schema.json when the fetch carries it, else the bundle's keys), every leaf drawn from the data. `mask` is the whole of what changes the drawing: `paths` (case-insensitive, against `section › key › …`) and `values` mask a leaf — the row then carries only the value's LENGTH, so the secret never reaches a view; `collapse_over` folds any object or list larger than this into one counted row (the keyboard's default clipboard list is 476 clips, and pasted tokens live in clips). MEASURED on the real bundle 2026-09-30: every token, password, key, WireGuard profile and clip text masks; ~200 rows draw. A declaration with no pattern, or a pattern that does not compile, masks EVERY leaf (InfoMask.maskAll). #626's hand-listed sections moved, none was lost: person → setup (contact card), tokens → connect (credentials held), repos → setup, fleet → setup (the cockpit), vault/wireguard/store were links and their surfaces are unchanged.

infos._doc_schema: #713 THE SCHEMA THE VAULT JSON FILLS, so Infos draws every section and every field — filled (its value, through the mask above) or `empty` — and not only what one export happens to carry. Sections and labels are cloud-vault Shared/configs/schema.json#sections (schema_version 1); a section's fields are the resolver items of Shared/configs/<section>/sources.json#items, as `›`-joined paths (a node carrying a resolver `kind` is one field). cloud-vault is private and CI cannot read it, so the skeleton is carried here; test-account-four-tabs.sh F re-derives it from the vault whenever cloud-vault sits beside this repo and goes red on any drift. A field or section the bundle carries beyond this skeleton is still drawn, after the declared ones. #727: the vault has more sections than schema.json lists — a Shared/configs/<dir>/sources.json not yet in schema.json is a STAGED section (apps, peers: adding one to schema.json needs a keyed emit.py rebuild), and #713 derived the skeleton from schema.json alone, so the owner's declared app list never reached Infos. The skeleton is now EVERY sources.json directory: schema.json's sections in its order, then the staged ones by id, each marked `staged` and labelled by its id. F's drift check walks the directories, not the list, so a section can no longer be skipped. `render: apps` also draws the section's declared apps one by one (name, package, store of record, installed on this phone) and `route` is the Store page it links to (Phone Apps, whose Declared view installs what is missing).

ui._doc_wireguard_profiles: The four EXPORTABLE tunnel profiles, mirrored from vault/Shared/Providers/C_TOOLS-INFRA/c0-wireguard/termux-public/config-v{4,6}-{split,full}. SEPARATE FROM wireguard_default ON PURPOSE: wireguard_default seeds the in-app form and is what matchesCloudPreset() compares against, so folding these values into it would make every existing install read as drifted and prompt to replace a config the user may have hand-built. Nothing here is ever written to WireGuardPrefs; it is render-only, consumed by WireGuardProfiles.kt to emit wg-quick text for export. The phone is a SINGLE-TUNNEL mesh spoke (Android allows one active WG profile), so each profile is ONE merged config carrying BOTH meshes as two peers - there are 4 files, not 8. Both v6 prefixes appear on every Address line and they are NOT interchangeable: fd0c:1d00::9 is the wg0 identity and fd0c:1d01::9 is the wg-public identity. Sending fd0c:1d00:: traffic to oci-analytics is cryptokey-dropped there (its allowed source for this phone is fd0c:1d01::9), which is the 14-30s happy-eyeballs stall. MTU is 1380 and the gcp-proxy endpoint is udp/443 (redirected to 51820) because port filtering eats 51820; DNS is mesh-only. No private key is present or permitted here - the export omits it by design. The two PUBLIC-VPN profiles (Cloudflare WARP, Proton VPN, #614) are declared SEPARATELY in ui.wireguard_external_profiles so this vault-locked block stays exactly the guard's four. SEPARATE FROM wireguard_default ON PURPOSE: wireguard_default seeds the in-app form and is what matchesCloudPreset() compares against, so folding these values into it would make every existing install read as drifted and prompt to replace a config the user may have hand-built. Nothing here is ever written to WireGuardPrefs; it is render-only, consumed by WireGuardProfiles.kt to emit wg-quick text for export. peers.comment:
gcp-proxy - all IPv4 internet (gcp-proxy has no v6 egress) + wg0 mesh v6. IPv4 default is 0.0.0.0/0 MINUS this peer's own endpoint 35.226.147.64/32 (excluded-route split): a literal 0.0.0.0/0 would route the handshake into the tunnel it is establishing (#523).
# fd0c:1d00::/64 MUST be listed here even though v6 egress goes to
# oci-analytics: it is more specific than the other peer's ::/0, so mesh v6
# reaches the hub directly instead of being handed to oci-analytics (which

peers.name: gcp-proxy

peers.name: oci-analytics

profiles.comment: wg-v6-full - IPv6-only wifi, FULL tunnel for IPv4 (everything v4 via oci-analytics). NOT ::/0: a v6 default route covers this peer's own v6 endpoint, so the handshake is routed into the tunnel it is trying to establish and the peer never comes up (#523). Nothing is lost - native-v6 sites are directly reachable and IPv4-only hosts ride 0.0.0.0/0 through the tunnel.

peers.name: gcp-proxy

The v6 side is deliberately two specific prefixes, never ::/0: the mesh (fd0c:1d01::/64, which is also the DNS64 resolver fd0c:1d01::1) and the NAT64 prefix that resolver synthesises into - CUSTOM here, not the well-known 64:ff9b::/96

ui._doc_wireguard_external_profiles: #614. PUBLIC-VPN profiles the phone can also run — Cloudflare WARP and Proton VPN — kept in a SEPARATE block from wireguard_profiles ON PURPOSE: wireguard_profiles is derived from and guard-locked to the cloud-infra vault dist (cloud-android-wireguard-profiles-guard.py compares it profile-for-profile), and these two are NOT in the vault — they are the user's own commercial-VPN accounts. Same shape as a mesh profile so WireGuardProfiles.kt renders them identically, but declared as IMPORT-TEMPLATES: empty public_key/endpoint/Address and an empty PrivateKey (per-account credentials are never baked into the app), filled by the WireGuard screen's Import .conf affordance. Data-driven: add an entry here and it becomes a selectable, exportable profile with no Kotlin change.

ui._doc_dns: #740 FLEET DNS — the ONE declaration behind Configs ▸ Setup ▸ Network ▸ DNS (network/FleetDns.kt reads it baked as BuildConfig.UI_DNS_B64; no resolver address is a Kotlin literal). Fleet apps and engines resolve through the Android system resolver, so the setting is applied ONCE, at the SuperApp's VPN: the chosen preset becomes the DNS server list of the Cloud Mesh tunnel (WireGuardPrefs.toTunnelConfig → VpnService.Builder.addDnsServer in the net-wg engine), and every app routed by that VPN inherits it. CODE OVER BRIEF: firestack (FirestackTunnelService) is compiled but NOT the active engine — FirewallController drives the interim drain engine, its WG proxy registration and protect() are still TODO — so firestack's own DNS layer (DoH/DoT, per-domain split) is not reachable yet; this block is shaped so it can feed that layer the day it is. `kind` decides the mapping: mirror = no servers on the VPN (Android uses the underlying network's resolver and its Private DNS); public = `servers` then `fallback`, in order; private = the fleet resolver, which is the Cloud Mesh page's DNS field (wireguard_default.interface_dns on a fresh install — hickory-dns on the hub), followed ONLY when `fallback_allowed` by the presets the user orders from `fallback_choices`. `encryption: dot_opportunistic` is honest about where encryption happens: Android's resolver upgrades to DNS-over-TLS against these IPs when Private DNS is Automatic, which the page checks and can set. A preset with `available: false` is drawn disabled with its `unavailable_reason` and can never be chosen or used as a fallback. `mesh_zones` are hickory-dns's own zones (cloud-u-containers infra-net_hickory-dns build.json dns.zones): when the mesh is up those names route to the fleet resolver whatever the preset (FleetDns.upstreamsFor — the page's test lookup uses it); the VPN carries one ordered list, so for the system resolver that split holds only under the private presets until firestack's DNS layer is active. `test_names` are what the page's Test lookup resolves.

dns._doc_self_resolvers: #794 Fleet code that talks DNS ITSELF instead of asking Android's resolver, so the preset in force does not decide where those lookups go. Each entry is inside a tree 1_cicd/src/data/dns-resolver-guard.json allows (that guard fails the build on any other), and the DNS page's Bridges list flags the app `pkg` names with `what` and `how`. Everything else in the fleet resolves through Android: Kotlin/Java code directly, terminal shells through their 127.0.0.1 SystemDnsBridge, bundled binaries through libs:sysdns ResolverProxy.

self_resolvers.what: the DNS page's Test lookup and server probes
self_resolvers.how: plain DNS over UDP straight to each listed server (FleetDns.query), so the page can name the one that answers
its own DoH / DoT / dns53 transports — compiled into the firewall, not the engine the VPN runs today

only the mesh's own bootstrap names (the relay host): the pinned answer from data/mesh.json and DoH by IP (ui.mesh_transport.doh) when the system resolver fails or disagrees with the pin; every other name stays on the preset

dns._doc_mesh_down: #751 The choice also holds while Cloud Mesh is DOWN. The WireGuard engine (Cloud-Lib-Net-Wg) owns the phone's one VPN slot; when no mesh tunnel is up it carries the choice as a PEERLESS tunnel named `tunnel_name`: these addresses, the preset's DNS servers, no route, so every app's lookups go to the chosen resolver and all other traffic falls through to the underlying network exactly as it does outside a split mesh. The fleet resolver is unreachable without the mesh, so Private with fallbacks uses its fallbacks alone, and Private only keeps the fleet resolver with a route to nowhere: lookups fail, none leaks to the local network. Mirror releases the slot.
dns._doc_android_private_dns: Replica of Android's own Settings ▸ Private DNS menu. `id` is the literal value of Settings.Global private_dns_mode; `label` is what Android shows. `hostname_suggestions` pre-fill the provider field.

android_private_dns._doc_private_presets_require: #794 Android's Automatic (opportunistic) Private DNS sends EVERY lookup over DoT to a validated public server (1.1.1.1, dns.google) before any plain server in the list is asked, so with a public fallback on the VPN the fleet resolver is never reached and mesh names answer public. A private preset is only in effect in this mode; FleetDns.verdict says so and data/device-tuning.json (android_private_dns_off) applies it.

presets.subtitle: The fleet uses whatever Android is set to — the VPN carries no DNS server of its own.

presets.label: Public open
presets.subtitle: Cloudflare, falling back to Google. Plain DNS.

presets.label: Public encrypted
presets.subtitle: Cloudflare, falling back to Google, over DNS-over-TLS (Android Private DNS must be Automatic).

presets.label: Cloudflare WARP
presets.subtitle: WARP is a WireGuard tunnel to Cloudflare with device registration.
presets.unavailable_reason: Needs a second WireGuard upstream beside the mesh inside the one VPN slot. The running mesh engine (net-wg GoBackend) is one interface with one key and address set, and firestack — which can carry several WireGuard proxies — is not the active engine yet.

presets.subtitle: The fleet resolver over the mesh, nothing else. Mesh down = lookups fail.

presets.label: Private with fallbacks
presets.subtitle: The fleet resolver first, then the fallbacks you order below.

ui._doc_mesh_page: #877 THE declaration of the Cloud Mesh page (network/WireGuardFragment.kt hosts it, network/mesh/* draws it): the tab strip's page ids and labels, each page's controls with their defaults, and the numbers the live readout uses. Baked as BuildConfig.UI_MESH_PAGE_B64; network/mesh/MeshDecl.kt parses it and test-mesh-page.sh holds it equal to the code in both directions. A control has EITHER an `engine` id - one of the calls MeshStore dispatches to, which are the EXISTING paths (WgState.backend setState/getState/getStatistics, WireGuardPrefs, AccountMesh, FleetDns) - OR an `unsupported` reason, which the page shows beside the control, disabled: a control the engine cannot honour is never silent and never a no-op (a `read.*` engine id reports a state the engine can read but not write, and must carry `unsupported` for the write). `default_from` names a seed in another declaration (dns.default_preset = ui.dns.default_preset; interface_mtu / tunnel_name / interface_address = ui.wireguard_default) so a default is stated once. `handshake.fresh_s` / `stale_s` bound the peer light: a handshake no older than fresh is FRESH, up to stale is AGING (both green), older than stale is STALE and none yet is NONE (both amber, the second says 'none'). A control's `group` is the heading it sits under on its page (string mesh_group_<id>). `nat64_marker` is the hextet that marks a /96 allowed-IP as the NAT64 prefix on the Routes page. Polling (`poll_ms`) runs only while the page is RESUMED; `latency_every_ticks` thins the latency probe to every Nth poll.

mesh_page._doc_tabs: #1074 The strip: three TABS over the sections in `pages` (a section is a former page; its controls and rows are declared there, once). Status = every config in effect (state, interface, endpoint, transport, handshakes, traffic, latency, DNS, active profile, the Cloudflare transport) then the routes and the peers; Profile = the profile table where one is chosen (with the Cloudflare WARP / One cards), then ALL former Controls (tunnel connect/reconnect, start-up, DNS preset, MTU, keepalive, identity, key, fallbacks); Logs = the journal. A section lives in exactly one tab; test-mesh-page.sh and MeshDeclTest hold that every section is reachable.
mesh_page._doc_startup: #1120 ROOT CAUSE of the greyed-out Start-up switches (Profile tab): auto_boot / auto_wifi / auto_mobile / kill_switch were declared with an `unsupported` text and no engine call (kill_switch only a read-only one), so ControlRow drew them disabled for ever - nothing in the app could act on them. They now act: network/MeshIntent.kt keeps the owner's intent (connected until Disconnect, default ON) and the three conditions (all default ON), network/MeshSupervisorRunner.kt reconnects on network change / tunnel drop / process start / reboot while the intent holds, and the kill switch (Android lockdown) and the Status page's Always-on VPN switch are changed through the privileged shell channel (AlwaysOnVpn.kt, `settings put secure always_on_vpn_app|always_on_vpn_lockdown`); with no channel armed the switch says why and opens Android's VPN settings.
mesh_page._doc_previous_controls: #1074 THE GUARD: every control id the page had before the three-tab reorganisation. Each must still be declared in `pages` AND be reachable from a tab (MeshDeclTest, test-mesh-page.sh T10), so a control cannot silently disappear in a later reshuffle. A control removed on purpose is removed here in the same commit, with the reason in the commit message. New controls are not listed (they are guarded by their own tests).
mesh_page._doc_cloudflare: #1074 Cloudflare as a Cloud Mesh transport (network/CloudflareWarp.kt). WARP (no Zero Trust): the phone generates a key pair, POSTs its PUBLIC key to the WARP API at api/api_version/reg (the open registration logic the MIT-licensed wgcf documents; written here, nothing vendored) and runs the WireGuard config in the answer on the existing engine; the private key and device token live only in CfKeyStore (EncryptedSharedPreferences). Cloudflare One (Zero Trust tunnel into the mesh, team `one.team`): the team login opens as a Custom Tab on <team>.cloudflareaccess.com<login_path>, the Access token it returns enrols the device, and the answer is the config. `one.enabled` is false while the server side is not applied (#994: Zero Trust routes + device enrolment policy, waiting on owner approval): the page then shows 'waiting on Zero Trust apply' and the enrol button stays disabled. Flip `one.enabled` to true in the commit that follows #994's apply and the option lights up; nothing else changes.

ui._doc_mesh_transport: THE FALLBACK LADDER of Cloud Mesh (network/MeshTransport.kt reads it baked as BuildConfig.UI_MESH_TRANSPORT_B64; the Status tab's `transport` row and the mesh badge show which rung carries the tunnel, Controls > Fallbacks picks the mode, holds the relay key and runs Test fallbacks). Public Wi-Fi that blocks DNS, port 53 or the mesh's UDP ports leaves WireGuard without a handshake. A connect walks: (1) Direct UDP on the configured endpoints; a peer endpoint that is a NAME is resolved by the system resolver, its answer checked against the PINNED map (data/mesh.json::bootstrap.pinned_hosts, derived by cloud-infra's derive-mesh-snapshot.ts from the Cloudflare zone, never typed here), then the pinned answer, then DoH by IP (`doh`, so DoH itself needs no DNS); (2) when no handshake arrives within `handshake_wait_ms`, the TLS-443 relay: the wstunnel server named by bootstrap.relay, reached at an address from the same ladder (system answer only when it agrees with the pin), real TLS on 443 with SNI and the certificate checked against the relay's name, in the WireGuard engine (Cloud-Lib-Net-Wg, MeshRelay) so its socket is protect()ed from the tunnel; every hub bootstrap.relay.routes reaches gets its endpoint pointed at 127.0.0.1:<relay_listen_base + n>. `mode`: auto = the ladder, direct = UDP only, relay = the relay at once. The relay key is the server's WSTUNNEL_PATH_PREFIX (sops, cloud-u-containers infra-net_wireguard-mesh-ws-tunnel): pasted once, kept in wireguard_prefs as a secret-class key, never baked, logged or exported. `probe_timeout_ms` bounds each rung of Test fallbacks.
ui._doc_wireguard_default: Seeds the Configs/WireGuard form on first run. The phone is a single-tunnel mesh spoke (Android allows one active WG profile) carrying TWO peers / two meshes — gcp-proxy wg0 (10.0.0.0/24) and oci-analytics wg-public (10.1.0.0/24), mirrored from vault/.../wireguard/termux-public/config. The network-popup Mesh section probes each peer's hub (.1 of its allowed_ips) as a separate light. peer.public_key IS seeded — WireGuard PUBLIC keys are non-secret (the hubs' public identity, already in the public cloud repo). interface_private_key + peer.preshared_key are NOT seeded (the private key is the credential — Pillar 7): generate via the in-app Generate Keypair button, or import the merged .conf / paste manually. All values are FIRST-RUN defaults, user-editable at runtime via WireGuardFragment (Add/Remove Peer; persisted in WireGuardPrefs). ALIGNED WITH THE VAULT, which is the config that demonstrably works on phones — this block had drifted into handing out three defects at once: gcp-proxy on udp/51820 (a filterable port; the hub redirects udp/443 to it precisely so the tunnel survives carrier port filtering), MTU 1280 (below the 1380 the working profiles use), and 1.1.1.1/1.0.0.1 in the resolver list (a mesh-only-DNS policy violation — a public resolver in the list means mesh names resolve off-mesh, or not at all). It now matches ui.wireguard_profiles, which was already vault-aligned; the two must not disagree, since one seeds the form and the other is what the export writes. oci-analytics stays on :51821, which is its real listen port.
ui._doc_modes: Global UI mode (Apps <-> Admin). No longer a toolbar toggle: Apps and Admin are ordinary PAGES of the sections that have both, marked "facet": true. Opening one sets the mode, so the Home grid, drawer and bottom-nav icon variants (icon_apps/icon_admin) follow the page just opened. Sections with tiles_shared ignore the mode. Persisted via ModePrefs (regular SharedPreferences - not encrypted, it's just a view-pref).

THE KEY RULE (VaultCockpit.meshKey): the key stored is the picked device's own — a profile key whose public half is not the device's declared wg_public_key is refused, a phone key that is not the device's is refused, and when neither the bundle nor the phone holds the device's key the report names the Generate/import path that exists. agent_auth._doc: #790 the terminals' agent CLIs, logged in from the declared profile instead of a /login typed into one phone. For each fleet app in `apps` (fleet-config.json ids), Account reads `settings › app › <store> › NAME` as the declared value at env.NAME's vault path (AccountFleet.derive, applied to S and L as read, never written into either file), so server → runtime and the new-phone migration import it over the #783 FleetConfig contract like any other app setting. NAME is the environment variable the CLI reads; the terminal writes the store to $HOME/<ab_cloud-terminal-store/store.json::agent_auth.env_file> (0600) and every login sources it. A value the profile declares at that settings key itself wins; a null token (ai › tokens › claude is `subscription, token: null` until a `claude setup-token` token is put in a vault sops store) adds nothing.

derived_settings._doc: #802 the browser's autofill profile, from the declared profile: Account reads `settings › browser › browser_autofill › KEY` as the vault subtree at keys.KEY (an object or list travels as its JSON text; AccountFleet.derive, the #790 mechanism), so server → runtime and the new-phone migration import it over the #783 FleetConfig contract into the browser's encrypted, secret-class store, and Drift shows it masked. The browser maps the raw subtree itself (libs:browser BrowserProfile.fromVaultBundle). Cards are not in the bundle and never travel this way.

#mail cloud-mail's accounts, from the declared profile: Account reads `settings › mail › sterna_account › vault_mail` as the vault's whole `mail` section (accounts, passwords, endpoints) as JSON text, and `vault_owner` as about.profile.email, the address that names the domain and the account made current (the same rules as VaultCockpit.mailAccounts / mailEndpoints / ownerEmail), so the new-phone migration and Fleet Setup import them over the #783 FleetConfig contract into the mail app's secret-class keys. On start the mail app (core/data VaultMailImport) adds every declared account through AccountStore.add — each password encrypted into its own pw_<id> slot by that API — makes the owner's current and REMOVES both keys: the section is in transit, never kept.

cockpit._doc_vault_fields: #781 THE FIELD MAP: every field Profiles shows (ui.profile.infos.schema, `section › field`) → the app(s) that use it at runtime (`apps`, cockpit section ids) and whether those apps HOLD it live (`held`: Runtime reads it and Drift compares it) or only take it as input when applying (`held` false). A field no phone app uses has `apps` [] and a `why`, so Profiles and Runtime never disagree about what exists. test-account-vault-fields.sh holds this map EQUAL to the schema (both ways), every app id to a declared section, every held field's section to its app's `vault`, and every item of the cloud-vault sources beside it to a schema field. AccountRuntime counts each app's declared / reported / missing from it.

ui._doc_app_urls: #572 THE ONE DECLARATION behind the long-press menu's URLs section (AppUrls.kt derives, AppLongPressMenu.kt draws; neither holds a URL). OUR apps: an external_apps entry names the backend service it talks to in `service` — a `name` in data/services_public.json (public_url + private_dns) or data/services_private.json (private_dns only) — and the menu shows that row's public URL and private (mesh) URL, read from the snapshot regen.sh already keeps. The endpoints are never restated here, so they cannot drift from the infra; an app with no `service` (or one the snapshot no longer lists) gets no URL rows. `public_scheme` / `private_scheme` prefix the two: the snapshot stores hosts without a scheme, and the mesh's Caddy upstreams are plain HTTP on the WireGuard interface. PHONE apps: ONE derivation, first hit wins — (1) the app's own manifest <meta-data>, the first of `website_meta_keys` it declares that holds an http(s) URL; (2) the page of the store that really installed it (getInstallSourceInfo), from `installer_pages` — {pkg} is substituted, and its `label` names the row so a store page is never passed off as the vendor's website. Nothing found = the row is not drawn, never guessed. Not derived: F-Droid's index `homepage` (needs the repo index, which is a network fetch per long-press) — its store page in (2) links to it. PUBLISHED SITES (#677): a static site (GitHub Pages) is neither a mesh service nor an installed package, so an external_apps entry names it in `site` — the LABEL of a link in data/linktree.json, the portal snapshot that already holds every github.io URL. The URL is read from there, never restated and never built from a repo name (mymaps-navigation and mymaps-mytrips do not follow <owner>.github.io/<repo>); a label that matches no link, or two links with different URLs, yields no row. NOT SILENT: when nothing is drawn the section says why, and says it two different ways — `URL missing:` for a declared service/site that does not resolve, `No URL kind for this app:` when nothing is declared or found at all. test-menu-urls-declarative.sh fails on any literal http(s) URL in the menu code, on a `service` that names no snapshot row, and on a `site` that names no single linktree link. LNKTREE PAGES: a kind=entry panel (Cloud ▸ Lnktree pages) reads its target through LnktreeTargets from `site` (a linktree.json label, as above), `registry` (a key of `registry_sites`: the `webapp` URL of that code in 0_registry/projects-repos.json, copied by key and checked against it by test-lnktree-row.sh) or `repo` + `path` under `repo_base`. An entry with none is `planned` and drawn greyed.
ui._doc_external_apps: Companion Android apps the SuperApp launches instead of rendering an in-app fragment. A tile target of `extapp:<id>` (see ui.sections[communication]) resolves here: MainActivity.launchExternalApp tries the app's package (hub_package); if not installed it snacks '<label> not installed' (install via Configs ▸ Constellation, which pulls the APK from GHCR). Fully data-driven: package ids live ONLY here, never in Kotlin. The ex-Cloud-Comms forks are now STANDALONE constellation apps (ea_cloud-{dialer,chat,mail,matrix}, each its own ship-cloud-<id>.yml CI); the cloud-comms hub is decommissioned (archived). They keep their com.diegonmarcos.comms.<fork> package ids. install_apk_url points at the shared rolling 'latest' GitHub release asset cloud-comms-<fork>.apk (uploaded by build.sh gh-release-fork per each fork's build.json::release.gh_release), mirroring how the other standalone apps use /releases/download/latest/. forkless (forks:{}), so extapp:<id> resolves straight to hub_package. `folder` names the ui.phone_folders id this app classifies into, and it is the ONLY place that fact is written: PhoneFolders.loadFromBuildConfig derives a `pkg:` keyword for hub_package, alt_package, install_package and every fork from it. Our own apps used to be listed twice — identity here, an identical `pkg:` keyword there — with nothing tying the copies together, which is how an app could be installable and sectionless at the same time. Adding a constellation app is now one entry here and no second edit; omitting `folder` leaves the app in the sink, so test-app-identity-resolves.sh requires it.

Cloud Office (ac_cloud-office, com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice) — OUR build, as of 2026-09-16, and THIS IS THE ONE EDIT THE PREVIOUS _doc SAID TO MAKE: "WHEN THE SOURCE BUILD FIRST PUBLISHES: hub_package/install_package/install_apk_url move here in one edit". Until run 35043058309 these three fields named com.collabora.libreoffice and Cloud-Sheets.apk, and that was correct — ac_cloud-office's build.host was null, ship-cloud-office.yml exited 1 rather than mirror an app it no longer described, and the only office artefact in existence was Collabora's own signed APK republished under our release name. Leaving these fields behind is now the failure the old _doc warned about with the signs reversed: hub_package is how the launcher decides whether the app is on the phone, and install_apk_url is what the tile downloads, so the Office tile would pull 267 MB of a third party's build over a metered connection and install a package nothing else in this fleet names. package read from ac_cloud-office/build.json::android.application_id and confirmed against the PUBLISHED artefact, not the source: its AndroidManifest.xml was pulled out of the ZIP by byte range, inflated, and com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice found in the AXML string pool while com.collabora.libreoffice and org.collabora.app are both absent. install_apk_url mirrors ac_cloud-office/build.json::release.gh_release. THE OWNER'S PHONE KEEPS THE OLD COLLABORA OFFICE UNTIL HE UNINSTALLS IT BY HAND — a different package id is a different app to Android — which is also why Cloud-Sheets.apk stays on the release rather than being tidied away. folder=prod_docs is the taxonomy half of the same record: PhoneFolders derives the pkg: keyword from it, so NO literal keyword for com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice may be added to ui.phone_folders, and test-app-identity-resolves.sh T8b fails on exactly that.

external_apps._doc_abi: install_apk_url names the arm64 asset, which is the ONLY shape this schema has — all 19 entries carry one flat URL. Cloud Writer is the first companion published in two ABI variants (Cloud-Writer.apk / Cloud-Writer-x86_64.apk, both in the generated data/constellation-fleet.json under `assets`), so on an x86_64 device a flat arm64 URL is #43 again: INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS.
